<p>Straddling the <a href="/wiki/Tropic_of_Cancer" title="Tropic of Cancer">Tropic of Cancer</a>, Bangladesh's climate is tropical, with a mild winter from October to March and a hot, humid summer from March to June. The country has never recorded an air temperature below 0&#160;°C (32&#160;°F), with a record low of 1.1&#160;°C (34.0&#160;°F) in the northwest city of <a href="/wiki/Dinajpur" title="Dinajpur">Dinajpur</a> on 3 February 1905.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup> A warm and humid <a href="/wiki/Monsoon" title="Monsoon">monsoon</a> season lasts from June to October and supplies most of the country's rainfall. Natural calamities, such as <a href="/wiki/Floods_in_Bangladesh" title="Floods in Bangladesh">floods</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tropical_cyclone" title="Tropical cyclone">tropical cyclones</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tornado" title="Tornado">tornadoes</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Tidal_bore" title="Tidal bore">tidal bores</a> occur almost every year,<sup id="cite_ref-NatDis_178-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NatDis-178">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup> combined with the effects of <a href="/wiki/Deforestation" title="Deforestation">deforestation</a>, <a href="/wiki/Soils_retrogression_and_degradation" class="mw-redirect" title="Soils retrogression and degradation">soil degradation</a> and <a href="/wiki/Erosion" title="Erosion">erosion</a>. The <a href="/wiki/List_of_Bangladesh_tropical_cyclones" title="List of Bangladesh tropical cyclones">cyclones</a> of 1970 and 1991 were particularly devastating, the <a href="/wiki/1991_Bangladesh_cyclone" title="1991 Bangladesh cyclone">latter</a> killing approximately 140,000 people.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In September 1998, Bangladesh saw the <a href="/wiki/1998_Bangladesh_floods" class="mw-redirect" title="1998 Bangladesh floods">most severe flooding</a> in modern history, after which two-thirds of the country went underwater, along with a death toll of 1,000.<sup id="cite_ref-EWG_180-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EWG-180">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> As a result of various international and national level initiatives in disaster risk reduction, human toll and economic damage from floods and cyclones have come down over the years.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/2007_South_Asian_floods" title="2007 South Asian floods">2007 South Asian floods</a> ravaged areas across the country, leaving five million people displaced, had a death toll around 500.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh is recognised to be one of the countries most <a href="/wiki/Climate_change_vulnerability" title="Climate change vulnerability">vulnerable to climate change</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup> Over the course of a century, 508 cyclones have affected the Bay of Bengal region, 17 percent of which are believed to have caused landfall in Bangladesh.<sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> Natural hazards that come from increased rainfall, rising sea levels, and tropical cyclones are expected to increase as the climate changes, each seriously affecting agriculture, water and food security, human health, and shelter.<sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup> It is estimated that by 2050, a 3 feet rise in sea levels will inundate some 20 percent of the land and displace more than 30 million people.<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup> To address the <a href="/wiki/Sea_level_rise" title="Sea level rise">sea level rise</a> threat in Bangladesh, the Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 has been launched.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_188-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-188">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Biodiversity">Biodiversity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Wildlife_of_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Wildlife of Bangladesh">Wildlife of Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fauna_of_Bangladesh" title="Fauna of Bangladesh">Fauna of Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Bengal_Tiger_gets_down_in_a_shallow_canal_in_Sundarban.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Bengal_Tiger_gets_down_in_a_shallow_canal_in_Sundarban.jpg/220px-Bengal_Tiger_gets_down_in_a_shallow_canal_in_Sundarban.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Bengal_Tiger_gets_down_in_a_shallow_canal_in_Sundarban.jpg/330px-Bengal_Tiger_gets_down_in_a_shallow_canal_in_Sundarban.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Bengal_Tiger_gets_down_in_a_shallow_canal_in_Sundarban.jpg/440px-Bengal_Tiger_gets_down_in_a_shallow_canal_in_Sundarban.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1067" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Bengal_Tiger_gets_down_in_a_shallow_canal_in_Sundarban.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>A <a href="/wiki/Bengal_tiger" title="Bengal tiger">Bengal tiger</a>, the national animal, in the Sundarbans</div></div></div>
<p>Bangladesh is located in the <a href="/wiki/Indomalayan_realm" title="Indomalayan realm">Indomalayan realm</a>, and lies within four terrestrial ecoregions: <a href="/wiki/Lower_Gangetic_Plains_moist_deciduous_forests" title="Lower Gangetic Plains moist deciduous forests">Lower Gangetic Plains moist deciduous forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mizoram%E2%80%93Manipur%E2%80%93Kachin_rain_forests" title="Mizoram–Manipur–Kachin rain forests">Mizoram–Manipur–Kachin rain forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sundarbans_freshwater_swamp_forests" class="mw-redirect" title="Sundarbans freshwater swamp forests">Sundarbans freshwater swamp forests</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Sundarbans_mangroves" class="mw-redirect" title="Sundarbans mangroves">Sundarbans mangroves</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-DinersteinOlson2017_190-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-190">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup> Its ecology includes a long sea coastline, numerous <a href="/wiki/List_of_rivers_in_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="List of rivers in Bangladesh">rivers and tributaries</a>, lakes, <a href="/wiki/Wetland" title="Wetland">wetlands</a>, evergreen forests, semi evergreen forests, hill forests, moist <a href="/wiki/Deciduous_forest" class="mw-redirect" title="Deciduous forest">deciduous forests</a>, freshwater swamp forests and flat land with tall grass. The Bangladesh Plain is famous for its fertile <a href="/wiki/Alluvial" class="mw-redirect" title="Alluvial">alluvial</a> soil which supports extensive cultivation. The country is dominated by lush vegetation, with villages often buried in groves of <a href="/wiki/Mango" title="Mango">mango</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jackfruit" title="Jackfruit">jackfruit</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bamboo" title="Bamboo">bamboo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Betel_nut" class="mw-redirect" title="Betel nut">betel nut</a>, <a href="/wiki/Coconut" title="Coconut">coconut</a> and <a href="/wiki/Date_palm" title="Date palm">date palm</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-global.britannica.com_191-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-global.britannica.com-191">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup> The country has up to 6000 species of plant life, including 5000 flowering plants.<sup id="cite_ref-192" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-192">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup> Water bodies and wetland systems provide a habitat for many aquatic plants. <a href="/wiki/Nymphaeaceae" title="Nymphaeaceae">Water lilies</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nelumbo_nucifera" title="Nelumbo nucifera">lotuses</a> grow vividly during the monsoon season. The country has <a href="/wiki/List_of_protected_areas_of_Bangladesh" title="List of protected areas of Bangladesh">50 wildlife sanctuaries</a>.
</p><p>Bangladesh is home to much of the <a href="/wiki/Sundarbans" title="Sundarbans">Sundarbans</a>, the world's largest <a href="/wiki/Mangrove_forest" title="Mangrove forest">mangrove forest</a>, covering an area of 6,000 square kilometres (2,300&#160;sq&#160;mi) in the southwest littoral region. It is divided into three protected sanctuaries–the <a href="/wiki/Sundarbans_South_Wildlife_Sanctuary" title="Sundarbans South Wildlife Sanctuary">South</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sundarbans_East_Wildlife_Sanctuary" title="Sundarbans East Wildlife Sanctuary">East</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sundarbans_West_Wildlife_Sanctuary" title="Sundarbans West Wildlife Sanctuary">West</a> zones. The forest is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The northeastern Sylhet region is home to haor wetlands, a unique ecosystem. It also includes <a href="/wiki/Tropical_and_subtropical_coniferous_forests" title="Tropical and subtropical coniferous forests">tropical and subtropical coniferous forests</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Freshwater_swamp_forest" title="Freshwater swamp forest">freshwater swamp forest</a>, and mixed deciduous forests. The southeastern <a href="/wiki/Chittagong_Division" title="Chittagong Division">Chittagong region</a> covers evergreen and semi-evergreen hilly jungles. Central Bangladesh includes the plainland Sal forest running along with the districts of Gazipur, <a href="/wiki/Tangail" title="Tangail">Tangail</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mymensingh" title="Mymensingh">Mymensingh</a>. <a href="/wiki/St._Martin%27s_Island" title="St. Martin&#39;s Island">St. Martin's Island</a> is the only <a href="/wiki/Coral_reef" title="Coral reef">coral reef</a> in the country.
</p><p>Bangladesh has an abundance of <a href="/wiki/Wildlife_in_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Wildlife in Bangladesh">wildlife</a> in its forests, marshes, woodlands and hills.<sup id="cite_ref-global.britannica.com_191-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-global.britannica.com-191">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup> The vast majority of animals dwell within a habitat of 150,000 square kilometres (58,000&#160;sq&#160;mi).<sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Bengal_tiger" title="Bengal tiger">Bengal tiger</a>, <a href="/wiki/Clouded_leopard" title="Clouded leopard">clouded leopard</a>, <a href="/wiki/Saltwater_crocodile" title="Saltwater crocodile">saltwater crocodile</a>, <a href="/wiki/Black_panther" title="Black panther">black panther</a> and <a href="/wiki/Fishing_cat" title="Fishing cat">fishing cat</a> are among the chief predators in the Sundarbans.<sup id="cite_ref-194" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-194">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup> Northern and eastern Bangladesh is home to the <a href="/wiki/Asian_elephant" title="Asian elephant">Asian elephant</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hoolock_gibbon" title="Hoolock gibbon">hoolock gibbon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Asian_black_bear" title="Asian black bear">Asian black bear</a> and <a href="/wiki/Oriental_pied_hornbill" title="Oriental pied hornbill">oriental pied hornbill</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-bearprojectbd.weebly.com_195-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bearprojectbd.weebly.com-195">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Chital" title="Chital">Chital</a> deer are widely seen in southwestern woodlands. Other animals include the <a href="/wiki/Black_giant_squirrel" title="Black giant squirrel">black giant squirrel</a>, <a href="/wiki/Capped_langur" title="Capped langur">capped langur</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bengal_fox" title="Bengal fox">Bengal fox</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sambar_deer" title="Sambar deer">sambar deer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jungle_cat" title="Jungle cat">jungle cat</a>, <a href="/wiki/King_cobra" title="King cobra">king cobra</a>, <a href="/wiki/Wild_boar" title="Wild boar">wild boar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mongoose" title="Mongoose">mongooses</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pangolin" title="Pangolin">pangolins</a>, <a href="/wiki/Python_(genus)" title="Python (genus)">pythons</a> and <a href="/wiki/Asian_water_monitor" title="Asian water monitor">water monitors</a>. Bangladesh has one of the largest populations of <a href="/wiki/Irrawaddy_dolphins" class="mw-redirect" title="Irrawaddy dolphins">Irrawaddy dolphins</a> and <a href="/wiki/South_Asian_river_dolphin" title="South Asian river dolphin">Ganges dolphins</a>. A 2009 census found 6,000 Irrawaddy dolphins inhabiting the littoral rivers of Bangladesh.<sup id="cite_ref-196" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-196">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup> The country has numerous species of <a href="/wiki/Amphibian" title="Amphibian">amphibians</a> (53), reptiles (139), <a href="/wiki/Marine_reptile" title="Marine reptile">marine reptiles</a> (19) and <a href="/wiki/Marine_mammal" title="Marine mammal">marine mammals</a> (5). It also has <a href="/wiki/List_of_birds_of_Bangladesh" title="List of birds of Bangladesh">628 species of birds</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Several animals became extinct in Bangladesh during the last century, including the one-horned and two-horned <a href="/wiki/Rhinoceros" title="Rhinoceros">rhinoceros</a> and common <a href="/wiki/Peafowl" title="Peafowl">peafowl</a>. The human population is concentrated in urban areas, limiting deforestation to a certain extent. Rapid urban growth has threatened natural habitats. Although many areas are protected under law, some Bangladeshi wildlife is threatened by this growth. The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Environment_Conservation_Act" class="mw-redirect" title="Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act">Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act</a> was enacted in 1995. The government has designated several regions as <a href="/wiki/Ecologically_Critical_Area" title="Ecologically Critical Area">Ecologically Critical Areas</a>, including wetlands, forests, and rivers. The <a href="/wiki/Sundarbans_tiger_project" class="mw-redirect" title="Sundarbans tiger project">Sundarbans tiger project</a> and the Bangladesh Bear Project are among the key initiatives to strengthen conservation.<sup id="cite_ref-bearprojectbd.weebly.com_195-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bearprojectbd.weebly.com-195">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup> It ratified the Rio <a href="/wiki/Convention_on_Biological_Diversity" title="Convention on Biological Diversity">Convention on Biological Diversity</a> on 3 May 1994.<sup id="cite_ref-cbd.int_198-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cbd.int-198">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup> As of 2014<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bangladesh&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, the country was set to revise its <a href="/wiki/Biodiversity_action_plan" title="Biodiversity action plan">National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cbd.int_198-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cbd.int-198">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Politics_and_government">Politics and government</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Bangladesh" title="Politics of Bangladesh">Politics of Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Bangladesh" title="Government of Bangladesh">Government of Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangabhaban.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Bangabhaban.jpg/220px-Bangabhaban.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="130" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Bangabhaban.jpg/330px-Bangabhaban.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Bangabhaban.jpg/440px-Bangabhaban.jpg 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="472" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangabhaban.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Bangabhaban" title="Bangabhaban">Bangabhaban</a> (literally <i>Bengal House</i>) is the <a href="/wiki/Presidential_palace" title="Presidential palace">presidential palace</a> of Bangladesh. It was originally a house for the <a href="/wiki/Viceroy_of_India" class="mw-redirect" title="Viceroy of India">Viceroy of India</a> and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_governors_of_Bengal_Presidency" title="List of governors of Bengal Presidency">Governor of Bengal</a>.</div></div></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladesh_National_Parliament_in_2022.04.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Bangladesh_National_Parliament_in_2022.04.jpg/220px-Bangladesh_National_Parliament_in_2022.04.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Bangladesh_National_Parliament_in_2022.04.jpg/330px-Bangladesh_National_Parliament_in_2022.04.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Bangladesh_National_Parliament_in_2022.04.jpg/440px-Bangladesh_National_Parliament_in_2022.04.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="3000" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladesh_National_Parliament_in_2022.04.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Jatiya_Sangsad_Bhaban" title="Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban">National Parliament</a> building in <a href="/wiki/Sher-e-Bangla_Nagar" title="Sher-e-Bangla Nagar">Sher-e-Bangla Nagar</a>, a neighborhood named after the first <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Bengal" title="Prime Minister of Bengal">Prime Minister of Bengal</a>.</div></div></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladesh_Supreme_Court.jpg" class="image"><img alt="Long, white, domed building" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Bangladesh_Supreme_Court.jpg/220px-Bangladesh_Supreme_Court.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Bangladesh_Supreme_Court.jpg/330px-Bangladesh_Supreme_Court.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Bangladesh_Supreme_Court.jpg/440px-Bangladesh_Supreme_Court.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1023" data-file-height="767" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladesh_Supreme_Court.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Bangladesh" title="Supreme Court of Bangladesh">Supreme Court of Bangladesh</a></div></div></div>
<p>Bangladesh is a <i><a href="/wiki/De_jure" title="De jure">de jure</a></i> <a href="/wiki/Representative_democracy" title="Representative democracy">representative democracy</a> under its <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Bangladesh" title="Constitution of Bangladesh">constitution</a>, with a <a href="/wiki/Westminster_system" title="Westminster system">Westminster</a>-style <a href="/wiki/Unitary_authority" title="Unitary authority">unitary</a> <a href="/wiki/Parliamentary_republic" title="Parliamentary republic">parliamentary republic</a> that has <a href="/wiki/Universal_suffrage" title="Universal suffrage">universal suffrage</a>. The head of government is the Prime Minister, who is invited to form a government every five years. The President invites the leader of the largest party in parliament to become Prime Minister of the world's fifth-largest democracy.<sup id="cite_ref-199" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-199">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh experienced a <a href="/wiki/Two_party_system" class="mw-redirect" title="Two party system">two party system</a> between 1990 and 2014, when the <a href="/wiki/Awami_League" title="Awami League">Awami League</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Nationalist_Party" title="Bangladesh Nationalist Party">Bangladesh Nationalist Party</a> (BNP) alternated in power. During this period, elections were managed by a neutral <a href="/wiki/Caretaker_government_of_Bangladesh" title="Caretaker government of Bangladesh">caretaker government</a>. But the caretaker government was abolished by the Awami League government in 2011.
</p><p>One of the key aspects of Bangladeshi politics is the "spirit of the liberation war", which refers to the ideals of the liberation movement during the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War" title="Bangladesh Liberation War">Bangladesh Liberation War</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-200" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-200">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup> The Proclamation of Independence enunciated the values of "equality, human dignity and social justice". In 1972, the constitution included a <a href="/wiki/Bill_of_rights" title="Bill of rights">bill of rights</a> and declared "nationalism, socialism, democracy and <a href="/wiki/Secularity" title="Secularity">secularity</a>" as the principles of government policy. Socialism was later de-emphasised and neglected by successive governments. Bangladesh has a market-based economy. To many Bangladeshis, especially in the younger generation, the spirit of the liberation war is a vision for a society based on civil liberties, human rights, the rule of law and good governance.<sup id="cite_ref-201" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-201">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Legislature" title="Legislature">Legislative</a>: The <a href="/wiki/Jatiya_Sangshad" class="mw-redirect" title="Jatiya Sangshad">Jatiya Sangshad</a> (National Parliament) is the <a href="/wiki/Unicameral" class="mw-redirect" title="Unicameral">unicameral</a> parliament. It has 350 <a href="/wiki/Member_of_parliament" title="Member of parliament">Members of Parliament</a> (MPs), including 300 MPs elected on the <a href="/wiki/First_past_the_post" class="mw-redirect" title="First past the post">first past the post</a> system and 50 MPs appointed to reserved seats for <a href="/wiki/Women%27s_empowerment" title="Women&#39;s empowerment">women's empowerment</a>. <a href="/wiki/Article_70_of_the_Constitution_of_Bangladesh" title="Article 70 of the Constitution of Bangladesh">Article 70 of the Constitution of Bangladesh</a> forbids MPs from voting against their party. However, several laws proposed independently by MPs have been transformed into legislation, including the anti-torture law.<sup id="cite_ref-202" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-202">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup> The parliament is presided over by the <a href="/wiki/Speaker_of_the_Jatiya_Sangsad" title="Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad">Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad</a>, who is second in line to the president as per the constitution. There is also a Deputy Speaker. When a president is incapable of performing duties (i.e. due to illness), the Speaker steps in as <a href="/wiki/Acting_President" class="mw-redirect" title="Acting President">Acting President</a> and the Deputy Speaker becomes Acting Speaker. A recurring proposal suggests that the Deputy Speaker should be an opposition member.<sup id="cite_ref-203" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-203">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Executive_(government)" title="Executive (government)">Executive</a>: The <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Bangladesh" title="Government of Bangladesh">Government of Bangladesh</a> is overseen by a <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Bangladesh" title="Cabinet of Bangladesh">cabinet</a> headed by the <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Bangladesh" title="Prime Minister of Bangladesh">Prime Minister of Bangladesh</a>. The tenure of a parliamentary government is five years. The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Civil_Service" title="Bangladesh Civil Service">Bangladesh Civil Service</a> assists the cabinet in running the government. Recruitment for the civil service is based on a public examination. In theory, the civil service should be a meritocracy. But a disputed quota system coupled with politicisation and preference for seniority have allegedly affected the civil service's meritocracy.<sup id="cite_ref-204" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-204">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/President_of_Bangladesh" title="President of Bangladesh">President of Bangladesh</a> is the ceremonial head of state<sup id="cite_ref-205" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-205">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup> whose powers include signing bills passed by parliament into law. The President is elected by the parliament and has a five-year term. Under the constitution, the president acts on the prime minister's advice. The President is the Supreme Commander of the Bangladesh Armed Forces and the chancellor of all universities.</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Laws_in_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Laws in Bangladesh">Judiciary</a>: The <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Bangladesh" title="Supreme Court of Bangladesh">Supreme Court of Bangladesh</a> is the highest court of the land, followed by the <a href="/wiki/High_Court_Division" class="mw-redirect" title="High Court Division">High Court</a> and Appellate Divisions. The head of the judiciary is the <a href="/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_Bangladesh" title="Chief Justice of Bangladesh">Chief Justice of Bangladesh</a>, who sits on the Supreme Court. The courts have wide latitude in <a href="/wiki/Judicial_review_in_Bangladesh" title="Judicial review in Bangladesh">judicial review</a>, and judicial <a href="/wiki/Precedent" title="Precedent">precedent</a> is supported by Article 111 of the constitution. The <a href="/wiki/Judiciary_of_Bangladesh" title="Judiciary of Bangladesh">judiciary</a> includes district and metropolitan courts divided into civil and criminal courts. Due to a shortage of judges, the judiciary has a large backlog. The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Judicial_Service_Commission" title="Bangladesh Judicial Service Commission">Bangladesh Judicial Service Commission</a> is responsible for judicial appointments, salaries, and discipline.</li></ul>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Armed_Forces" title="Bangladesh Armed Forces">Bangladesh Armed Forces</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladesh_Army_FM90_Crotale_SAM._(38169460305).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Bangladesh_Army_FM90_Crotale_SAM._%2838169460305%29.jpg/220px-Bangladesh_Army_FM90_Crotale_SAM._%2838169460305%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="144" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Bangladesh_Army_FM90_Crotale_SAM._%2838169460305%29.jpg/330px-Bangladesh_Army_FM90_Crotale_SAM._%2838169460305%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Bangladesh_Army_FM90_Crotale_SAM._%2838169460305%29.jpg/440px-Bangladesh_Army_FM90_Crotale_SAM._%2838169460305%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2909" data-file-height="1906" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladesh_Army_FM90_Crotale_SAM._(38169460305).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Bangladesh's <a href="/wiki/FM-90" class="mw-redirect" title="FM-90">FM-90</a> air defence missile system, modelled on the <a href="/wiki/Crotale_(missile)" title="Crotale (missile)">Crotale</a>.</div></div></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:262px;"><a href="/wiki/File:BangladeshMilitaryUN_PeacekeepingForce.jpg" class="image"><img alt="World map, indicating where the Bangladeshi UN peacekeeping force is stationed" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/BangladeshMilitaryUN_PeacekeepingForce.jpg/260px-BangladeshMilitaryUN_PeacekeepingForce.jpg" decoding="async" width="260" height="163" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/BangladeshMilitaryUN_PeacekeepingForce.jpg/390px-BangladeshMilitaryUN_PeacekeepingForce.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/BangladeshMilitaryUN_PeacekeepingForce.jpg/520px-BangladeshMilitaryUN_PeacekeepingForce.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1178" data-file-height="738" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:BangladeshMilitaryUN_PeacekeepingForce.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Map of <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_UN_Peacekeeping_Force" title="Bangladesh UN Peacekeeping Force">Bangladesh UN Peacekeeping Force</a> deployments.</div></div></div>
<p>The Bangladesh Armed Forces have inherited the institutional framework of the <a href="/wiki/British_military" class="mw-redirect" title="British military">British military</a> and the <a href="/wiki/British_Indian_Army" title="British Indian Army">British Indian Army</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-206" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-206">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> It was formed in 1971 from the military regiments of East Pakistan. In 2022, the active personnel strength of the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Army" title="Bangladesh Army">Bangladesh Army</a> was around 250,000,<sup id="cite_ref-IISS_207-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IISS-207">&#91;207&#93;</a></sup> excluding the Air Force and the Navy (24,000).<sup id="cite_ref-208" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-208">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup> In addition to traditional defence roles, the military has supported civil authorities in disaster relief and provided internal security during periods of political unrest. For many years, Bangladesh has been the world's largest contributor to <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_peacekeeping" title="United Nations peacekeeping">UN peacekeeping forces</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Military_budget_of_Bangladesh" title="Military budget of Bangladesh">military budget of Bangladesh</a> accounts for 1.3% of GDP, amounting to US$4.3 billion in 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-209" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-209">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-210" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-210">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Navy" title="Bangladesh Navy">Bangladesh Navy</a>, one of the largest in the Bay of Bengal, includes a <a href="/wiki/List_of_active_ships_of_the_Bangladesh_Navy" class="mw-redirect" title="List of active ships of the Bangladesh Navy">fleet</a> of frigates, submarines, corvettes and other vessels. The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Air_Force" title="Bangladesh Air Force">Bangladesh Air Force</a> has a <a href="/wiki/List_of_active_Bangladesh_military_aircraft" title="List of active Bangladesh military aircraft">small fleet</a> of multi-role combat aircraft, including the <a href="/wiki/MiG-29" class="mw-redirect" title="MiG-29">MiG-29</a> and <a href="/wiki/Chengdu_J-7" title="Chengdu J-7">Chengdu-F7</a>. Most of Bangladesh's military equipment comes from China.<sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup>  In recent years, Bangladesh and India have increased joint military exercises, high level visits of military leaders, <a href="/wiki/Counter-terrorism" class="mw-redirect" title="Counter-terrorism">counter-terrorism</a> cooperation and intelligence sharing. Bangladesh is vital to ensuring stability and security in <a href="/wiki/Northeast_India" title="Northeast India">northeast India</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-212" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-212">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-213" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-213">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh's strategic importance in the eastern subcontinent hinges on its proximity to China, its frontier with Burma, the separation of mainland and northeast India, and its maritime territory in the Bay of Bengal.<sup id="cite_ref-214" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-214">&#91;214&#93;</a></sup> In 2002, Bangladesh and China signed a Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA) which the governments of both countries said will "institutionalize the existing accords in defence sector and also to rationalize the existing piecemeal agreements to enhance cooperation in training, maintenance and in some areas of production".<sup id="cite_ref-215" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-215">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup> The United States has pursued negotiations with Bangladesh on a <a href="/wiki/Status_of_forces_agreement" title="Status of forces agreement">Status of Forces Agreement</a>, an <a href="/wiki/Acquisition_and_Cross-Servicing_Agreement" title="Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement">Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement</a> and a General Security of Military Information Agreement.<sup id="cite_ref-216" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-216">&#91;216&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-217" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-217">&#91;217&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218">&#91;218&#93;</a></sup> In 2019, Bangladesh ratified the UN <a href="/wiki/Treaty_on_the_Prohibition_of_Nuclear_Weapons" title="Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons">Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219">&#91;219&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_relations">Foreign relations</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Bangladesh" title="Foreign relations of Bangladesh">Foreign relations of Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate_John_Kerry_Visits_Bangladesh_(51104953309).png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate_John_Kerry_Visits_Bangladesh_%2851104953309%29.png/220px-Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate_John_Kerry_Visits_Bangladesh_%2851104953309%29.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="223" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate_John_Kerry_Visits_Bangladesh_%2851104953309%29.png/330px-Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate_John_Kerry_Visits_Bangladesh_%2851104953309%29.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate_John_Kerry_Visits_Bangladesh_%2851104953309%29.png/440px-Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate_John_Kerry_Visits_Bangladesh_%2851104953309%29.png 2x" data-file-width="1263" data-file-height="1280" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate_John_Kerry_Visits_Bangladesh_(51104953309).png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/U.S._Special_Presidential_Envoy_for_Climate" title="U.S. Special Presidential Envoy for Climate">U.S. Special Presidential Envoy for Climate</a> <a href="/wiki/John_Kerry" title="John Kerry">John Kerry</a> meeting Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina at her residence in Dhaka in April 2021</div></div></div>
<p>Bangladesh is considered a <a href="/wiki/Middle_power" title="Middle power">middle power</a> in <a href="/wiki/Global_politics" title="Global politics">global politics</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-220" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-220">&#91;220&#93;</a></sup> It plays an important role in the geopolitical affairs of the <a href="/wiki/Indo-Pacific" title="Indo-Pacific">Indo-Pacific</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-221" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-221">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup> due to its strategic location between South and Southeast Asia.<sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh joined the <a href="/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations" title="Commonwealth of Nations">Commonwealth of Nations</a> in 1972 and the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> in 1974.<sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup> It relies on <a href="/wiki/Multilateralism" title="Multilateralism">multilateral</a> diplomacy on issues like climate change, nuclear nonproliferation, trade policy and non-traditional security issues.<sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup> At the <a href="/wiki/World_Trade_Organization" title="World Trade Organization">WTO</a>, Bangladesh has used the dispute resolution mechanism to settle trade disputes with India and other countries.<sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh pioneered the creation of <a href="/wiki/South_Asian_Association_for_Regional_Cooperation" title="South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation">SAARC</a>, which has been the preeminent forum for regional diplomacy among the countries of the <a href="/wiki/Indian_subcontinent" title="Indian subcontinent">Indian subcontinent</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup> It joined the <a href="/wiki/Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation" title="Organisation of Islamic Cooperation">OIC</a>, an <a href="/wiki/Intergovernmental_organisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Intergovernmental organisation">intergovernmental organisation</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Muslim_world" title="Muslim world">Muslim world</a> in 1974,<sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228">&#91;228&#93;</a></sup> and is a founding member of the <a href="/wiki/Developing_8_Countries" class="mw-redirect" title="Developing 8 Countries">Developing 8 Countries</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229">&#91;229&#93;</a></sup> In recent years, Bangladesh has focused on promoting regional trade and transport links with support from the <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230">&#91;230&#93;</a></sup> Dhaka hosts the headquarters of <a href="/wiki/BIMSTEC" class="mw-redirect" title="BIMSTEC">BIMSTEC</a>, an organisation that brings together <a href="/wiki/Countries_dependent_on_the_Bay_of_Bengal" class="mw-redirect" title="Countries dependent on the Bay of Bengal">countries dependent on the Bay of Bengal</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Bangladesh%E2%80%93Myanmar_relations" title="Bangladesh–Myanmar relations">Relations</a> with neighbouring <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a> have been severely strained since 2016–2017, after over 700,000 <a href="/wiki/Rohingya_refugees_in_Bangladesh" title="Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh">Rohingya refugees</a> illegally entered Bangladesh fleeing persecution, <a href="/wiki/Ethnic_cleansing" title="Ethnic cleansing">ethnic cleansing</a>, <a href="/wiki/Genocide" title="Genocide">genocide</a>, and other atrocities in their native state.<sup id="cite_ref-RohingyaHRW_231-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-RohingyaHRW-231">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> The parliament, government, and civil society of Bangladesh have been at the forefront of <a href="/wiki/International_reaction_to_the_2016%E2%80%9317_Rohingya_exodus" class="mw-redirect" title="International reaction to the 2016–17 Rohingya exodus">international criticism</a> against Myanmar for military operations against the Rohingya, and have demanded their <a href="/wiki/Right_of_return" title="Right of return">right of return</a> to <a href="/wiki/Arakan" title="Arakan">Arakan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232">&#91;232&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233">&#91;233&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh shares an important <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh%E2%80%93India_relations" title="Bangladesh–India relations">bilateral and economic relationship</a> with its largest neighbour <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234">&#91;234&#93;</a></sup> which is often strained by <a href="/wiki/Water_politics_in_India" class="mw-redirect" title="Water politics in India">water politics</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Ganges_water_dispute" title="Ganges water dispute">Ganges</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Teesta_River#Water_sharing_challenge" title="Teesta River">Teesta</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-235" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-235">&#91;235&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-236" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-236">&#91;236&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Deaths_along_the_Bangladesh%E2%80%93India_border" title="Deaths along the Bangladesh–India border">border killings of Bangladeshi civilians</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup> Post-independent Bangladesh has continued to have a problematic relationship with Pakistan, mainly due to its denial of the <a href="/wiki/1971_Bangladesh_genocide" class="mw-redirect" title="1971 Bangladesh genocide">1971 Bangladesh genocide</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> It maintains a <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh-China_relations" class="mw-redirect" title="Bangladesh-China relations">warm relationship</a> with <a href="/wiki/China" title="China">China</a>, which is its largest trading partner, and the largest arms supplier.<sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241">&#91;241&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Japan" title="Japan">Japan</a> is Bangladesh's largest economic aid provider, and the two maintain a <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh%E2%80%93Japan_relations" title="Bangladesh–Japan relations">strategic and economic partnership</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup> Political relations with Middle Eastern countries are robust.<sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243">&#91;243&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh receives 59% of its remittances from the Middle East,<sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup> despite poor working conditions affecting over 4 million <a href="/wiki/Bangladeshis_in_the_Middle_East" title="Bangladeshis in the Middle East">Bangladeshi workers</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-245" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-245">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh plays a major role in <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">global climate</a> diplomacy as a leader of the <a href="/wiki/Climate_Vulnerable_Forum" title="Climate Vulnerable Forum">Climate Vulnerable Forum</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-246" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-246">&#91;246&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Civil_society">Civil society</span></h3>
<p>Since the colonial period, Bangladesh has had a prominent <a href="/wiki/Civil_society" title="Civil society">civil society</a>. There are various special interest groups, including <a href="/wiki/Non-governmental_organisations" class="mw-redirect" title="Non-governmental organisations">non-governmental organisations</a>, human rights organisations, professional associations, <a href="/wiki/Chamber_of_commerce" title="Chamber of commerce">chambers of commerce</a>, employers' associations and <a href="/wiki/Trade_unions" class="mw-redirect" title="Trade unions">trade unions</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-247" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-247">&#91;247&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/National_Human_Rights_Commission_of_Bangladesh" title="National Human Rights Commission of Bangladesh">National Human Rights Commission of Bangladesh</a> was set up in 2007. Notable human rights organisations and initiatives include the <a href="/wiki/Centre_for_Law_and_Mediation_(Bangladesh)" class="mw-redirect" title="Centre for Law and Mediation (Bangladesh)">Centre for Law and Mediation</a>, <a href="/wiki/Odhikar" title="Odhikar">Odhikar</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Alliance_for_Bangladesh_Worker_Safety" title="Alliance for Bangladesh Worker Safety">Alliance for Bangladesh Worker Safety</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Environmental_Lawyers_Association" title="Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association">Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Hindu_Buddhist_Christian_Unity_Council" title="Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council">Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council</a> and the <a href="/wiki/War_Crimes_Fact_Finding_Committee" title="War Crimes Fact Finding Committee">War Crimes Fact Finding Committee</a>. The world's largest international NGO <a href="/wiki/BRAC_(organisation)" title="BRAC (organisation)">BRAC</a> is based in Bangladesh. There have been concerns regarding the shrinking space for independent civil society in recent years,<sup id="cite_ref-248" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-248">&#91;248&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-249" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-249">&#91;249&#93;</a></sup> with commentators labelling the civil society movement dead under the authoritarianism of the Awami League.<sup id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-250">&#91;250&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Human_rights">Human rights</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_Bangladesh" title="Human rights in Bangladesh">Human rights in Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><a href="/wiki/File:R.A.B.jpg" class="image"><img alt="Armed men in black uniforms on a street" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/R.A.B.jpg/170px-R.A.B.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="254" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/R.A.B.jpg/255px-R.A.B.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a9/R.A.B.jpg 2x" data-file-width="306" data-file-height="458" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:R.A.B.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Rapid_Action_Battalion" title="Rapid Action Battalion">Rapid Action Battalion</a> has been sanctioned by the United States for human rights abuses</div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Torture" title="Torture">Torture</a> is banned by Article 35 (5) of the <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Bangladesh" title="Constitution of Bangladesh">Constitution of Bangladesh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-251" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-251">&#91;251&#93;</a></sup> Despite this constitutional ban, torture is rampantly used by Bangladesh's security forces. Bangladesh joined the <a href="/wiki/Convention_against_Torture" class="mw-redirect" title="Convention against Torture">Convention against Torture</a> in 1998; but it enacted its first anti-torture law, the <a href="/wiki/Torture_and_Custodial_Death_(Prevention)_Act" title="Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention) Act">Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention) Act</a>, in 2013. The first conviction under this law was announced in 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-252" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-252">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> Amnesty International <a href="/wiki/Prisoner_of_conscience" title="Prisoner of conscience">Prisoners of Conscience</a> from Bangladesh have included <a href="/wiki/Saber_Hossain_Chowdhury" title="Saber Hossain Chowdhury">Saber Hossain Chowdhury</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shahidul_Alam" title="Shahidul Alam">Shahidul Alam</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-253" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-253">&#91;253&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-254" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-254">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Digital_Security_Act" class="mw-redirect" title="Digital Security Act">Digital Security Act</a> of 2018 has greatly reduced <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_expression" class="mw-redirect" title="Freedom of expression">freedom of expression</a> in Bangladesh, particularly on the internet. The Digital Security Act has been used to target critics of the government and bureaucracy. Newspaper editorials have been demanding the repeal of the Digital Security Act.<sup id="cite_ref-255" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-255">&#91;255&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-256" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-256">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-257" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-257">&#91;257&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-258" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-258">&#91;258&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On <a href="/wiki/International_Human_Rights_Day" class="mw-redirect" title="International Human Rights Day">International Human Rights Day</a> in December 2021, the United States <a href="/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Treasury" title="United States Department of the Treasury">Department of Treasury</a> announced <a href="/wiki/Economic_sanctions" title="Economic sanctions">sanctions</a> on commanders of the <a href="/wiki/Rapid_Action_Battalion" title="Rapid Action Battalion">Rapid Action Battalion</a> for extrajudicial killings, torture and other human rights abuses.<sup id="cite_ref-259" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-259">&#91;259&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Freedom_House" title="Freedom House">Freedom House</a> has criticised the ruling party for human rights abuses, crackdown on opposition, mass media, and civil society through politicized enforcement.<sup id="cite_ref-260" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-260">&#91;260&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh is ranked "partly free" in <a href="/wiki/Freedom_House" title="Freedom House">Freedom House</a>'s <i><a href="/wiki/Freedom_in_the_World" title="Freedom in the World">Freedom in the World</a></i> report,<sup id="cite_ref-261" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-261">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup> but its <a href="/wiki/Press_freedom" class="mw-redirect" title="Press freedom">press freedom</a> has deteriorated from "free" to "not free" in recent years due to increasing pressure from the authoritarian government.<sup id="cite_ref-262" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-262">&#91;262&#93;</a></sup> According to the British <a href="/wiki/Economist_Intelligence_Unit" title="Economist Intelligence Unit">Economist Intelligence Unit</a>, the country has a <a href="/wiki/Hybrid_regime" title="Hybrid regime">hybrid regime</a>: the third of four rankings in its <a href="/wiki/Democracy_Index" title="Democracy Index">Democracy Index</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-263" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-263">&#91;263&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh was ranked 96th among 163 countries in the 2022 <a href="/wiki/Global_Peace_Index" title="Global Peace Index">Global Peace Index</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-264" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-264">&#91;264&#93;</a></sup> According to National Human Rights Commission, 70% of alleged human-rights violations are committed by law-enforcement agencies.<sup id="cite_ref-265" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-265">&#91;265&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Bangladesh" title="LGBT rights in Bangladesh">LGBT rights</a> are heavily suppressed by both government and society,<sup id="cite_ref-266" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-266">&#91;266&#93;</a></sup> as <a href="/wiki/Homosexuality" title="Homosexuality">homosexuality</a> is outlawed by section 377 of the criminal code (a legacy of the colonial period), and is punishable by a maximum of life imprisonment.<sup id="cite_ref-267" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-267">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-268" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-268">&#91;268&#93;</a></sup> However, Bangladesh recognises the <a href="/wiki/Third_gender" title="Third gender">third gender</a> and accords limited rights for <a href="/wiki/Transgender" title="Transgender">transgender</a> people.<sup id="cite_ref-269" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-269">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup> According to the 2016 Global Slavery Index, an estimated 1,531,300 people are enslaved in Bangladesh, or roughly 1% of the population.<sup id="cite_ref-270" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-270">&#91;270&#93;</a></sup> A number of slaves in Bangladesh are forced to work in the fish and shrimp industries.<sup id="cite_ref-271" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-271">&#91;271&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-272" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-272">&#91;272&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-273" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-273">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Corruption">Corruption</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Corruption_in_Bangladesh" title="Corruption in Bangladesh">Corruption in Bangladesh</a></div>
<p>Like for many developing countries, institutional corruption is a serious concern for Bangladesh. Bangladesh was ranked 146th among 180 countries on <a href="/wiki/Transparency_International" title="Transparency International">Transparency International</a>'s 2018 <a href="/wiki/Corruption_Perceptions_Index" title="Corruption Perceptions Index">Corruption Perceptions Index</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-274" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-274">&#91;274&#93;</a></sup> According to a survey conducted by the Bangladesh chapter of TI, in 2015, the level of bribery was equivalent to 3.7 percent of the national budget.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_275-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-275">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup> Land administration was the sector with the most bribery in 2015,<sup id="cite_ref-:3_275-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-275">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup> followed by education,<sup id="cite_ref-276" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-276">&#91;276&#93;</a></sup> police<sup id="cite_ref-277" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-277">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup>
and water supply.<sup id="cite_ref-278" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-278">&#91;278&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Anti_Corruption_Commission_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Anti Corruption Commission Bangladesh">Anti Corruption Commission</a> was formed in 2004, and it was active during the <a href="/wiki/2006%E2%80%9308_Bangladeshi_political_crisis" class="mw-redirect" title="2006–08 Bangladeshi political crisis">2006–08 Bangladeshi political crisis</a>, indicting many leading politicians, bureaucrats and businessmen for <a href="/wiki/Graft_(politics)" title="Graft (politics)">graft</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-279" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-279">&#91;279&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-280" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-280">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-281" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-281">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Economy">Economy</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Bangladesh" title="Economy of Bangladesh">Economy of Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="center"><div class="thumb tnone"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:702px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Panorama_2_of_Gulshan_2_skyline_from_Baridhara_Lake_Park.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Panorama_2_of_Gulshan_2_skyline_from_Baridhara_Lake_Park.jpg/700px-Panorama_2_of_Gulshan_2_skyline_from_Baridhara_Lake_Park.jpg" decoding="async" width="700" height="236" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Panorama_2_of_Gulshan_2_skyline_from_Baridhara_Lake_Park.jpg/1050px-Panorama_2_of_Gulshan_2_skyline_from_Baridhara_Lake_Park.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/Panorama_2_of_Gulshan_2_skyline_from_Baridhara_Lake_Park.jpg/1400px-Panorama_2_of_Gulshan_2_skyline_from_Baridhara_Lake_Park.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1599" data-file-height="539" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Panorama_2_of_Gulshan_2_skyline_from_Baridhara_Lake_Park.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Commercial offices and apartments blocks seen from a lakefront in <a href="/wiki/Dhaka" title="Dhaka">Dhaka</a></div></div></div></div>

<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Shah_Amanat_763.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Shah_Amanat_763.jpg/220px-Shah_Amanat_763.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Shah_Amanat_763.jpg/330px-Shah_Amanat_763.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Shah_Amanat_763.jpg/440px-Shah_Amanat_763.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5464" data-file-height="3640" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Shah_Amanat_763.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Chittagong" title="Chittagong">Chittagong</a> has the <a href="/wiki/Port_of_Chittagong" title="Port of Chittagong">busiest port</a> on the Bay of Bengal</div></div></div>
<p>Bangladesh is the second largest economy in South Asia after India.<sup id="cite_ref-282" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-282">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-scroll.in_283-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-scroll.in-283">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup> The country has outpaced India (of which it was a part until 1947) and Pakistan (of which it was a part until 1971) in terms of per capita income.<sup id="cite_ref-284" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-284">&#91;284&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-scroll.in_283-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-scroll.in-283">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup> According to the <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>, "When the newly independent country of Bangladesh was born on December 16, 1971, it was the second poorest country in the world—making the country's transformation over the next 50 years one of the great development stories. Since then, poverty has been cut in half at record speed. Enrolment in primary school is now nearly universal. Hundreds of thousands of women have entered the workforce. Steady progress has been made on maternal and child health. And the country is better buttressed against the destructive forces posed by climate change and natural disasters. Bangladesh's success comprises many moving parts—from investing in human capital to establishing macroeconomic stability. Building on this success, the country is now setting the stage for further economic growth and job creation by ramping up investments in energy, inland connectivity, urban projects, and transport infrastructure, as well as prioritizing climate change adaptation and disaster preparedness on its path toward sustainable growth".<sup id="cite_ref-285" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-285">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>After the <a href="/wiki/Partition_of_India" title="Partition of India">partition of India</a>, the region underwent a change in economic geography. In <a href="/wiki/East_Pakistan" title="East Pakistan">East Pakistan</a>, free market principles were generally accepted. The government promoted <a href="/wiki/Industrialization" class="mw-redirect" title="Industrialization">industrialization</a> to produce consumer goods as quickly as possible in order to avoid dependence on imports. Certain sectors, like public utilities, fell under state ownership.<sup id="cite_ref-286" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-286">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup> Demand for jute during the <a href="/wiki/Korean_War" title="Korean War">Korean War</a> led to the creation of the <a href="/wiki/Adamjee_Jute_Mills" title="Adamjee Jute Mills">Adamjee Jute Mills</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-287" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-287">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> which replaced jute mills in <a href="/wiki/Dundee" title="Dundee">Dundee</a> and Calcutta as the largest jute mill in the world. However, by the 1960s, East Pakistan's share of exports fell from 70% to 50% as <a href="/wiki/West_Pakistan" title="West Pakistan">West Pakistan</a> received the major portion of investments. Economic grievances played a key role in the pro-independence aspirations of East Pakistanis. During the initial five years of independence (1971-1975), newly created Bangladesh followed a socialist economy. In the late 1970s, socialist policies were largely reversed, industrial plants were returned to private owners, and private industry was increasingly promoted. The government set up <a href="/wiki/Export_processing_zone" class="mw-redirect" title="Export processing zone">export processing zones</a> to stimulate the export economy. Between 1991 and 1993, finance minister <a href="/wiki/Saifur_Rahman" class="mw-redirect" title="Saifur Rahman">Saifur Rahman</a> launched further reforms with support from the <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">IMF</a> which liberalized the economy and boosted industrial growth, services, and exports.<sup id="cite_ref-288" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-288">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup> By the late 1990s and early 2000s, the reform momentum lost steam due to chronic <a href="/wiki/Political_instability" class="mw-redirect" title="Political instability">political instability</a>. But the economy continued to grow.
</p><p>In 2022, Bangladesh had the second largest <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_foreign_exchange_reserves" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by foreign exchange reserves">foreign-exchange reserves</a> in South Asia. The reserves have boosted the government's spending capacity in spite of tax revenues forming only 7.7% of government revenue.<sup id="cite_ref-trade.gov_289-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-trade.gov-289">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup> A big chunk of investments have gone into the <a href="/wiki/Electric_power" title="Electric power">power</a> sector. In 2009, Bangladesh was experiencing daily blackouts several times a day. In 2022, the country achieved 100% electrification.<sup id="cite_ref-290" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-290">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-291" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-291">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-292" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-292">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup> One of the major anti-poverty schemes of the Bangladeshi government is the <a href="/wiki/Ashrayan_Project" title="Ashrayan Project">Ashrayan Project</a> which aims to eradicate homelessness by providing free housing.<sup id="cite_ref-293" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-293">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup> The poverty rate has gone down from 80% in 1971,<sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup> to 44.2% in 1991,<sup id="cite_ref-295" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup> to 12.9% in 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> The literacy rate stood at 74.66% in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-297" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-297">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh has a <a href="/wiki/Labor_force" class="mw-redirect" title="Labor force">labor force</a> of roughly 70 million,<sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup> which is the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_labour_force" title="List of countries by labour force">seventh-largest</a>; with an unemployment rate of 5.2% as of 2021<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bangladesh&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>.<sup id="cite_ref-299" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-299">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup> The government is setting up 100 special economic zones to attract <a href="/wiki/Foreign_direct_investment" title="Foreign direct investment">foreign direct investment</a> (FDI) and generate 10 million jobs.<sup id="cite_ref-300" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-300">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Investment_Development_Authority" title="Bangladesh Investment Development Authority">Bangladesh Investment Development Authority</a> (BIDA) and the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Economic_Zones_Authority" title="Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority">Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority</a> (BEZA) have been established to help investors in setting up factories; and to complement the longstanding <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Export_Processing_Zone_Authority" title="Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Authority">Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Authority</a> (BEPZA). The <a href="/wiki/Bangladeshi_taka" title="Bangladeshi taka">Bangladeshi taka</a> is the national currency. The service sector accounts for about 51.3% of total GDP and employs 39% of the workforce. The industrial sector accounts for 35.1% of GDP and employs 20.4% of the workforce. The <a href="/wiki/Agriculture_in_Bangladesh" title="Agriculture in Bangladesh">agriculture sector</a> makes up 13.6% of the economy but is the biggest employment sector, with 40.6% of the workforce.<sup id="cite_ref-trade.gov_289-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-trade.gov-289">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup> In agriculture, the country is a major producer of <a href="/wiki/Rice_production_in_Bangladesh" title="Rice production in Bangladesh">rice</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_fishes_in_Bangladesh" title="List of fishes in Bangladesh">fish</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tea_production_in_Bangladesh" title="Tea production in Bangladesh">tea</a>, fruits, vegetables, flowers,<sup id="cite_ref-301" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-301">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup> and jute. <a href="/wiki/Lobster" title="Lobster">Lobsters</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shrimp" title="Shrimp">shrimps</a> are some of Bangladesh's well known exports.<sup id="cite_ref-302" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-302">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Private_sector">Private sector</span></h3>
<p>The private sector accounts for 80% of GDP in comparison to the dwindling role of state-owned companies.<sup id="cite_ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh's economy is dominated by family-owned <a href="/wiki/List_of_companies_of_Bangladesh" title="List of companies of Bangladesh">conglomerates</a> and small and medium-sized businesses. Some of the largest publicly-traded companies in Bangladesh include <a href="/wiki/Beximco" class="mw-redirect" title="Beximco">Beximco</a>, <a href="/wiki/BRAC_Bank" class="mw-redirect" title="BRAC Bank">BRAC Bank</a>, <a href="/wiki/BSRM" title="BSRM">BSRM</a>, <a href="/wiki/GPH_Ispat" title="GPH Ispat">GPH Ispat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Grameenphone" title="Grameenphone">Grameenphone</a>, <a href="/wiki/Summit_Group" title="Summit Group">Summit Group</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Square_Pharmaceuticals" title="Square Pharmaceuticals">Square Pharmaceuticals</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-304" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-304">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> Capital markets include the <a href="/wiki/Dhaka_Stock_Exchange" title="Dhaka Stock Exchange">Dhaka Stock Exchange</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Chittagong_Stock_Exchange" title="Chittagong Stock Exchange">Chittagong Stock Exchange</a>. Its <a href="/wiki/Telecommunications_in_Bangladesh" title="Telecommunications in Bangladesh">telecommunications industry</a> is one of the world's fastest growing, with 171.854 million cellphone subscribers in January 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-305" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-305">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup> Over 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings come from the garments industry.<sup id="cite_ref-bdarea_7-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bdarea-7">&#91;7&#93;</a></sup> Other major industries include <a href="/wiki/Shipbuilding_in_Bangladesh" title="Shipbuilding in Bangladesh">shipbuilding</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry_in_Bangladesh" title="Pharmaceutical industry in Bangladesh">pharmaceuticals</a>, <a href="/wiki/Steel_industry_in_Bangladesh" title="Steel industry in Bangladesh">steel</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ceramics_industry_in_Bangladesh" title="Ceramics industry in Bangladesh">ceramics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Electronics_industry_in_Bangladesh" title="Electronics industry in Bangladesh">electronics</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Leather_industry_in_Bangladesh" title="Leather industry in Bangladesh">leather goods</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-306" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-306">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Aziz_Khan_(businessman)" title="Aziz Khan (businessman)">Muhammad Aziz Khan</a> became the first person from Bangladesh to be listed as a billionaire by <i><a href="/wiki/Forbes" title="Forbes">Forbes</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Infrastructure">Infrastructure</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a 1.5x,
