2x" data-file-width="5467" data-file-height="3114" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%8B%E0%A6%A7%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0_%E0%A6%86%E0%A6%97%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0_%E0%A6%A6%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%87_%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BE_%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%81.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Padma_Bridge" title="Padma Bridge">Padma Bridge</a> is a <a href="/wiki/List_of_road%E2%80%93rail_bridges" title="List of road–rail bridges">road-rail bridge</a> which spans the Bangladeshi branch of the <a href="/wiki/Ganges" title="Ganges">Ganges</a> that is known as the <a href="/wiki/Padma_River" title="Padma River">Padma River</a>. It is the longest bridge on the Ganges. When it was opened in June 2022, the bridge was expected to boost GDP by 1.23%.<sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>Since 2009, Bangladesh has embarked on a series of <a href="/wiki/List_of_megaprojects_in_Bangladesh" title="List of megaprojects in Bangladesh">megaprojects</a>. The 6.15&#160;km long Padma Bridge was built at a cost of US$3.86 billion.<sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup> The bridge was the first self-financed megaproject in the country's history.<sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup> Other megaprojects include the <a href="/wiki/Dhaka_Metro" class="mw-redirect" title="Dhaka Metro">Dhaka Metro</a>, <a href="/wiki/Karnaphuli_Tunnel" title="Karnaphuli Tunnel">Karnaphuli Tunnel</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dhaka_Elevated_Expressway" title="Dhaka Elevated Expressway">Dhaka Elevated Expressway</a> and <a href="/wiki/Chittagong_Elevated_Expressway" title="Chittagong Elevated Expressway">Chittagong Elevated Expressway</a>; as well as the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Delta_Plan" title="Bangladesh Delta Plan">Bangladesh Delta Plan</a> to mitigate the impact of climate change. 
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Tourism">Tourism</span></h3>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Tourism_in_Bangladesh" title="Tourism in Bangladesh">tourism industry</a> is expanding, contributing some 3.02% of total GDP.<sup id="cite_ref-311" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-311">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh's international tourism receipts in 2019 amounted to $391 million.<sup id="cite_ref-312" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-312">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup> The country has <a href="/wiki/List_of_World_Heritage_Sites_in_Bangladesh" title="List of World Heritage Sites in Bangladesh">three UNESCO World Heritage Sites</a> (<a href="/wiki/Historic_Mosque_City_of_Bagerhat" class="mw-redirect" title="Historic Mosque City of Bagerhat">the Mosque City</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ruins_of_the_Buddhist_Vihara_at_Paharpur" class="mw-redirect" title="Ruins of the Buddhist Vihara at Paharpur">the Paharpur Buddhist Ruins</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Sundarbans" title="Sundarbans">Sundarbans</a>) and five <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Site#Nominating_process" title="World Heritage Site">tentative-list</a> sites.<sup id="cite_ref-313" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-313">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup> Activities for tourists include <a href="/wiki/Angling" title="Angling">angling</a>, <a href="/wiki/Water_skiing" title="Water skiing">water skiing</a>, river cruising, hiking, <a href="/wiki/Rowing_(sport)" title="Rowing (sport)">rowing</a>, <a href="/wiki/Yachting" title="Yachting">yachting</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Sea_bathing" title="Sea bathing">sea bathing</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-lp_314-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lp-314">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-lp_web_315-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lp_web-315">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/World_Travel_and_Tourism_Council" title="World Travel and Tourism Council">World Travel and Tourism Council</a> (WTTC) reported in 2019 that the travel and tourism industry in Bangladesh directly generated 1,180,500 jobs in 2018 or 1.9% of the country's total employment.<sup id="cite_ref-2019_report_316-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2019_report-316">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup> According to the same report, Bangladesh experiences around 125,000 international tourist arrivals per year.<sup id="cite_ref-2019_report_316-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2019_report-316">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup> Domestic spending generated 97.7 percent of direct travel and tourism gross domestic product (GDP) in 2012.<sup id="cite_ref-2013_report_317-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2013_report-317">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Energy_and_electricity">Energy and electricity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Electricity_sector_in_Bangladesh" title="Electricity sector in Bangladesh">Electricity sector in Bangladesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Energy_policy_of_Bangladesh" title="Energy policy of Bangladesh">Energy policy of Bangladesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Power_Development_Board" title="Bangladesh Power Development Board">Bangladesh Power Development Board</a>, <a href="/wiki/Natural_gas_and_petroleum_in_Bangladesh" title="Natural gas and petroleum in Bangladesh">Natural gas and petroleum in Bangladesh</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Petrobangla" title="Petrobangla">Petrobangla</a></div>
<p>Bangladesh is gradually transitioning to a <a href="/wiki/Green_economy" title="Green economy">green economy</a>. Currently, it has the largest off-grid solar power programme in the world, benefiting 20 million people.<sup id="cite_ref-318" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-318">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup> An <a href="/wiki/Electric_car" title="Electric car">electric car</a> called the <i>Palki</i> is being developed for production in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup> The government has reduced tariffs for the purchase of electric cars.<sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Biogas" title="Biogas">Biogas</a> is being used to produce organic fertilizer.<sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh continues to have huge untapped reserves of <a href="/wiki/Natural_gas" title="Natural gas">natural gas</a>, particularly in its maritime territory in the Bay of Bengal.<sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup> The success ratio of finding gas wells in the country stands at 3:5:1, meaning one commercial deposit is found in every three explored zones.<sup id="cite_ref-auto6_324-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto6-324">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> The success ratio is well above the global average.<sup id="cite_ref-auto6_324-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto6-324">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> A lack of exploration and decreasing proven reserves have forced Bangladesh to import <a href="/wiki/LNG" class="mw-redirect" title="LNG">LNG</a> from abroad, despite having substantially untapped gas reserves.<sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup> Gas shortages were further exasperated by the <a href="/wiki/Russia-Ukraine_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Russia-Ukraine War">Russia-Ukraine War</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>While <a href="/wiki/List_of_government-owned_companies_of_Bangladesh" title="List of government-owned companies of Bangladesh">government-owned companies in Bangladesh</a> generate nearly half of Bangladesh's electricity, privately-owned companies like the Summit Group and <a href="/wiki/Orion_Group" class="mw-redirect" title="Orion Group">Orion Group</a> are playing an increasingly important role in both generating electricity, and supplying machinery, reactors, and equipment.<sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh increased electricity production from 5 gigawatts in 2009 to 25.5 gigawatts in 2022. It plans to produce 50 <a href="/wiki/Gigawatts" class="mw-redirect" title="Gigawatts">gigawatts</a> by 2041. U.S. companies like <a href="/wiki/Chevron_Corporation" title="Chevron Corporation">Chevron</a> and <a href="/wiki/General_Electric" title="General Electric">General Electric</a> supply around 55% of Bangladesh's domestic natural gas production and are among the largest investors in power projects. 80% of Bangladesh's installed gas-fired power generation capacity comes from turbines manufactured in the United States.<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 4 October 2022, the national grid collapsed and plunged the whole country into a nationwide blackout. The grid resumed operations after eight hours. The government's investigation focused on technical failure, negligence, and possible sabotage. The investigation found that grid capacity has not kept up with the expansion of electricity generation and the opening of new power plants.<sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup> Gas shortages were also to blame, including the lack of new gas sources and insufficient gas pipeline infrastructure. There was a shortage of natural gas because of the <a href="/wiki/2021%E2%80%93present_global_energy_crisis" class="mw-redirect" title="2021–present global energy crisis">2021–present global energy crisis</a> as 77 <a href="/wiki/Natural_gas_power_plant" class="mw-redirect" title="Natural gas power plant">natural gas power plants</a> had insufficient fuel to meet demand. The <a href="/wiki/Electricity_sector_in_Bangladesh" title="Electricity sector in Bangladesh">electricity sector in Bangladesh</a> is heavily reliant on natural gas.<sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup> Gas shortages forced the government to import <a href="/wiki/Liquified_natural_gas" class="mw-redirect" title="Liquified natural gas">LNG</a> from abroad. As a result, Texas-based Excelerate Energy opened Bangladesh's first floating LNG terminal in 2018 off the coast of <a href="/wiki/Maheshkhali_Island" title="Maheshkhali Island">Maheshkhali Island</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup> The Summit LNG Terminal was opened in 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup> The Government of Bangladesh has <a href="/wiki/Subsidized" class="mw-redirect" title="Subsidized">subsidized</a> LNG imports worth several billion dollars. Since October 2021, Bangladesh imported LNG for US$30-37 per million <a href="/wiki/British_thermal_unit" title="British thermal unit">Btu</a> which is 10 times the price it paid in May 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup>
The government stopped buying <a href="/wiki/Spot_price" class="mw-redirect" title="Spot price">spot price</a> LNG in June 2022. The country's <a href="/wiki/Forex" class="mw-redirect" title="Forex">forex</a> reserves declined due to surging fuel imports. Bangladesh imported 30% of its LNG on the <a href="/wiki/Spot_price" class="mw-redirect" title="Spot price">spot price</a> market in 2022, down from 40% in 2021. Bangladesh continues to trade in LNG on the <a href="/wiki/Futures_exchange" title="Futures exchange">futures exchange</a> markets.<sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Demographics">Demographics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Bangladesh" title="Demographics of Bangladesh">Demographics of Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Bengalis" title="Bengalis">Bengalis</a></div>
<table class="toccolours" style="width:15em;border-top-width:0;border-spacing: 0;float:right;clear:right;margin:0.5em 0 1em 0.5em;"><caption style="border-top:1px #aaa solid;border-left:1px #aaa solid;border-right:1px #aaa solid;background-color:lavender;padding:0.25em;font-weight:bold">Population (millions)</caption><tbody><tr style="font-size:95%"><th style="border-bottom:1px solid black;padding:1px;text-align:right"><abbr title="Per annum growth rate">±% p.a.</abbr></th></tr><tr><th style="text-align:center;padding:1px">1971 </th><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">67,800,000</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">—&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:center;padding:1px">1980 </th><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">80,600,000</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">+1.94%</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:center;padding:1px">1990 </th><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">105,300,001</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">+2.71%</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:center;padding:1px">2000 </th><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">129,600,000</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">+2.10%</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:center;padding:1px;border-bottom:1px solid #bbbbbb">2010</th><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px;border-bottom:1px solid #bbbbbb">148,700,000</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px;border-bottom:1px solid #bbbbbb">+1.38%</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:center;padding:1px">2012</th><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">161,100,200</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">+4.09%</td></tr><tr><th style="text-align:center;padding:1px">2022</th><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">165,160,000</td><td style="text-align:right;padding:1px">+0.25%</td></tr><tr><td colspan="3" style="border-top:1px solid black;font-size:85%;text-align:left">Source: OECD/World Bank<sup id="cite_ref-IEApop2011_337-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IEApop2011-337">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-dhakatribune1_6-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dhakatribune1-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>According to the <a href="/wiki/2022_Census_of_Bangladesh" title="2022 Census of Bangladesh">2022 Census</a>, Bangladesh has a population of 165.1 million,<sup id="cite_ref-populationcensus2022_8-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-populationcensus2022-8">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup> and is the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by population">eighth-most-populous country</a> in the world, the <a href="/wiki/List_of_Asian_countries_by_population" title="List of Asian countries by population">fifth-most populous country</a> in Asia, and the <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density" title="List of countries and dependencies by population density">most densely populated large country</a> in the world, with a headline <a href="/wiki/Population_density" title="Population density">population density</a> of 1,265 people/km<sup>2</sup> as of 2020<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bangladesh&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>.<sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup> Its <a href="/wiki/Total_fertility_rate" title="Total fertility rate">total fertility rate</a> (TFR), once among the highest in the world, has experienced a dramatic decline, from 5.5 in 1985, to 3.7 in 1995, all the way down to 2.0 in 2020,<sup id="cite_ref-339" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-339">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup> which is below the <a href="/wiki/Sub-replacement_fertility" title="Sub-replacement fertility">sub-replacement fertility</a> of 2.1; due to the government promoting <a href="/wiki/Birth_control" title="Birth control">birth control</a> since the 1980s and increased education attainment of females.<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup> The vast majority of Bangladeshis live in <a href="/wiki/Rural_area" title="Rural area">rural areas</a>, with only 39% of the population living in <a href="/wiki/Urban_area" title="Urban area">urban areas</a> as of 2021<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bangladesh&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>.<sup id="cite_ref-341" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-341">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup> It has a <a href="/wiki/Median_age" class="mw-redirect" title="Median age">median age</a> of roughly 28 years, and its population is relatively young, with 26% of the total population aged 14 or younger,<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup> and merely 5% aged 65 and above.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh is an <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_ranked_by_ethnic_and_cultural_diversity_level" title="List of countries ranked by ethnic and cultural diversity level">ethnically and culturally homogeneous society</a>, as <a href="/wiki/Bengali_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Bengali people">Bengalis</a> form 99% of the population.<sup id="cite_ref-dhakatribune1_6-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dhakatribune1-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Adivasi" title="Adivasi">Adivasi</a> population includes the <a href="/wiki/Chakma_people" title="Chakma people">Chakmas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Marma_people" title="Marma people">Marmas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Santhal_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Santhal people">Santhals</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mru_people_(Mrucha)" class="mw-redirect" title="Mru people (Mrucha)">Mros</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tanchangya_people" title="Tanchangya people">Tanchangyas</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bawm_people" title="Bawm people">Bawms</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tripuri_people" title="Tripuri people">Tripuris</a>, <a href="/wiki/Khasi_people" title="Khasi people">Khasis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Khumi_people" title="Khumi people">Khumis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kuki_people" title="Kuki people">Kukis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Garo_people" title="Garo people">Garos</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bisnupriya_Manipuri_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Bisnupriya Manipuri people">Bisnupriya Manipuris</a>. The Chittagong Hill Tracts region experienced unrest and an <a href="/wiki/Chittagong_Hill_Tracts_conflict" title="Chittagong Hill Tracts conflict">insurgency</a> from 1975 to 1997 in an autonomy movement by its indigenous people. Although a peace accord was signed in 1997, the region remains militarised.<sup id="cite_ref-rashiduzzaman_344-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rashiduzzaman-344">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Urdu" title="Urdu">Urdu</a>-speaking <a href="/wiki/Stranded_Pakistanis" class="mw-redirect" title="Stranded Pakistanis">stranded Pakistanis</a> were given citizenship by the Supreme Court in 2008.<sup id="cite_ref-345" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-345">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh also hosts over 700,000 Rohingya refugees since 2017, giving it one of the largest refugee populations in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-RohingyaHRW_231-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-RohingyaHRW-231">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Urban_centres">Urban centres</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_and_towns_in_Bangladesh" title="List of cities and towns in Bangladesh">List of cities and towns in Bangladesh</a></div>
<p>Dhaka is Bangladesh's capital and largest city and is overseen by two city corporations who manage between them the northern and southern part of the city. There are 12 <a href="/wiki/List_of_City_Corporations_of_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="List of City Corporations of Bangladesh">city corporations</a> which hold mayoral elections: Dhaka South, Dhaka North, Chittagong, <a href="/wiki/Comilla" title="Comilla">Comilla</a>, <a href="/wiki/Khulna" title="Khulna">Khulna</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mymensingh" title="Mymensingh">Mymensingh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sylhet" title="Sylhet">Sylhet</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rajshahi" title="Rajshahi">Rajshahi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Barisal" title="Barisal">Barisal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rangpur,_Bangladesh" title="Rangpur, Bangladesh">Rangpur</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gazipur,_Dhaka_Division" class="mw-redirect" title="Gazipur, Dhaka Division">Gazipur</a> and <a href="/wiki/Narayanganj" title="Narayanganj">Narayanganj</a>. Mayors are elected for five-year terms. Altogether there are 506 urban centres in Bangladesh among which 43 cities have a population of more than 100,000.
</p>

<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Language">Language</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Languages_of_Bangladesh" title="Languages of Bangladesh">Languages of Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Chakma_Letter-Biplob_Rahman.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Chakma_Letter-Biplob_Rahman.jpg/220px-Chakma_Letter-Biplob_Rahman.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Chakma_Letter-Biplob_Rahman.jpg/330px-Chakma_Letter-Biplob_Rahman.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Chakma_Letter-Biplob_Rahman.jpg/440px-Chakma_Letter-Biplob_Rahman.jpg 2x" data-file-width="604" data-file-height="453" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Chakma_Letter-Biplob_Rahman.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Chakma_script" title="Chakma script">Chakma alphabets</a> are indigenous to the Chittagong Hill Tracts</div></div></div>
<p>The official and predominant language of Bangladesh is <a href="/wiki/Bengali_language" title="Bengali language">Bengali</a>, which is spoken by more than 98% of the population as their <a href="/wiki/First_language" title="First language">native language</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-LOG_346-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-LOG-346">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup> It is among the easternmost branches of the <a href="/wiki/Indo-European_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Indo-European language">Indo-European language</a> family, and is a part of the <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Indo-Aryan_languages" title="Eastern Indo-Aryan languages">Eastern Indo-Aryan languages</a>, which developed between the 10th and 13th centuries.<sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup> Bengali is described as a <a href="/wiki/Dialect_continuum" title="Dialect continuum">dialect continuum</a> where there are various <a href="/wiki/Bengali_dialects" title="Bengali dialects">dialects</a> spoken throughout the country. There is a <a href="/wiki/Diglossia" title="Diglossia">diglossia</a> in which much of the population are able to understand or speak Standard Colloquial Bengali and in their regional dialect,<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> such as <a href="/wiki/Chittagonian_language" title="Chittagonian language">Chittagonian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sylheti_language" title="Sylheti language">Sylheti</a> and which some linguists consider as separate languages; noted for their <a href="/wiki/Arabic" title="Arabic">Arab</a>-<a href="/wiki/Persian_language" title="Persian language">Persian</a> influences.<sup id="cite_ref-LOG_346-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-LOG-346">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/English_language" title="English language">English</a> plays an important role in Bangladesh's judicial and educational affairs, due to the country's history as part of the British Empire. It is widely spoken and commonly understood, and is taught as a compulsory subject in all <a href="/wiki/List_of_schools_in_Bangladesh" title="List of schools in Bangladesh">schools</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_colleges_in_Bangladesh" title="List of colleges in Bangladesh">colleges</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_universities_in_Bangladesh" title="List of universities in Bangladesh">universities</a>; while the English-medium educational system is widely attended.<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup> Tribal languages, although increasingly endangered, include the <a href="/wiki/Chakma_language" title="Chakma language">Chakma language</a>, another native Eastern Indo-Aryan language, spoken by the <a href="/wiki/Chakma_people" title="Chakma people">Chakma people</a>. Others include <a href="/wiki/Garo_language" title="Garo language">Garo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Meitei_language" title="Meitei language">Meitei</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kokborok" title="Kokborok">Kokborok</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rakhine_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Rakhine language">Rakhine</a>. Among the <a href="/wiki/Austroasiatic_languages" title="Austroasiatic languages">Austroasiatic languages</a>, the most spoken is the <a href="/wiki/Santali_language" title="Santali language">Santali language</a>, native to the <a href="/wiki/Santal_people" title="Santal people">Santal people</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Stranded_Pakistanis_in_Bangladesh" title="Stranded Pakistanis in Bangladesh">stranded Pakistanis</a> and some sections of the <a href="/wiki/Dhakaiyas" title="Dhakaiyas">Old Dhakaites</a> often use <a href="/wiki/Urdu" title="Urdu">Urdu</a> as their native tongue, although the usage of the latter remains highly reproached.<sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Religion">Religion</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Religion_in_Bangladesh" title="Religion in Bangladesh">Religion in Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Eid_Prayers_at_Barashalghar,_Debidwar,_Comilla.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Eid_Prayers_at_Barashalghar%2C_Debidwar%2C_Comilla.jpg/220px-Eid_Prayers_at_Barashalghar%2C_Debidwar%2C_Comilla.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Eid_Prayers_at_Barashalghar%2C_Debidwar%2C_Comilla.jpg/330px-Eid_Prayers_at_Barashalghar%2C_Debidwar%2C_Comilla.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Eid_Prayers_at_Barashalghar%2C_Debidwar%2C_Comilla.jpg/440px-Eid_Prayers_at_Barashalghar%2C_Debidwar%2C_Comilla.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2592" data-file-height="1944" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Eid_Prayers_at_Barashalghar,_Debidwar,_Comilla.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Eid_prayers" title="Eid prayers">Eid prayers</a> for Muslims at Barashalghar, <a href="/wiki/Debidwar_Upazila" title="Debidwar Upazila">Debidwar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Comilla" title="Comilla">Comilla</a></div></div></div>
<p>Bangladesh was constitutionally proclaimed as the first <a href="/wiki/Secular_state" title="Secular state">secular state</a> of South Asia in 1972. It grants <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_religion" title="Freedom of religion">freedom of religion</a> and claims to be "secular in practise", while establishing Islam as the <a href="/wiki/State_religion" title="State religion">state religion</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Secularism_353-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Secularism-353">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-constituteproject_354-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-constituteproject-354">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-aljazeera:1_355-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-aljazeera:1-355">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup> The constitution bans religion-based politics and discrimination, and proclaims equal recognition of people adhering to all faiths.<sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Bangladesh" title="Islam in Bangladesh">Islam</a> is the largest religion across the country, being followed by about 91.1% of the population.<sup id="cite_ref-dhakatribune1_6-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dhakatribune1-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-globalreligiousfutures1_357-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-globalreligiousfutures1-357">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-kbrs_358-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kbrs-358">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup> The vast majority of Bangladeshi citizens are <a href="/wiki/Bengali_Muslims" title="Bengali Muslims">Bengali Muslims</a>, adhering to <a href="/wiki/Sunni_Islam" title="Sunni Islam">Sunni Islam</a>. The country is the third-most populous Muslim-majority state in the world, and has the fourth-largest overall Muslim population.<sup id="cite_ref-359" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-359">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Hinduism_in_Bangladesh" title="Hinduism in Bangladesh">Hinduism</a> is followed by 7.9% of the population,<sup id="cite_ref-dhakatribune1_6-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dhakatribune1-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-globalreligiousfutures1_357-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-globalreligiousfutures1-357">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-kbrs_358-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kbrs-358">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup> mainly by the <a href="/wiki/Bengali_Hindus" title="Bengali Hindus">Bengali Hindus</a>, who form the country's second-largest religious group and the third-largest Hindu community globally; after those in India and Nepal. <a href="/wiki/Buddhism_in_Bangladesh" title="Buddhism in Bangladesh">Buddhism</a> is the third-largest religion, at 0.6% of the population. Bangladeshi Buddhists are concentrated among the tribal ethnic groups in the Chittagong Hill Tracts. At the same time, coastal Chittagong is home to many <a href="/wiki/Bengali_Buddhist" class="mw-redirect" title="Bengali Buddhist">Bengali Buddhists</a>. Christianity is the fourth-largest religion, at 0.3%, followed mainly by a small <a href="/wiki/Bengali_Christians" title="Bengali Christians">Bengali Christian</a> minority. While 0.1% practices other religions like <a href="/wiki/Animism" title="Animism">Animism</a> and <a href="/wiki/Irreligion" title="Irreligion">no religion</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-dhakatribune1_6-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dhakatribune1-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Education">Education</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Education_in_Bangladesh" title="Education in Bangladesh">Education in Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Literacy_rate_Bangladesh.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Literacy_rate_Bangladesh.png/220px-Literacy_rate_Bangladesh.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="223" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Literacy_rate_Bangladesh.png/330px-Literacy_rate_Bangladesh.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Literacy_rate_Bangladesh.png/440px-Literacy_rate_Bangladesh.png 2x" data-file-width="464" data-file-height="471" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Literacy_rate_Bangladesh.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Literacy rates in Bangladesh districts</div></div></div>
<p>Article (17) of the constitution states that all children shall receive free and compulsory education.<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup> Education in Bangladesh is overseen by the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Bangladesh)" title="Ministry of Education (Bangladesh)">Ministry of Education</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Primary_and_Mass_Education" title="Ministry of Primary and Mass Education">Ministry of Primary and Mass Education</a> is responsible for implementing policy for <a href="/wiki/Primary_education" title="Primary education">primary education</a> and state-funded schools at a local level. Primary and secondary education is <a href="/wiki/Compulsory_education" title="Compulsory education">compulsory</a>, and is financed by the state and free of charge in public schools. Bangladesh has a <a href="/wiki/Literacy_rate" class="mw-redirect" title="Literacy rate">literacy rate</a> of 74.7% percent as of 2019: 77.4% for males and 71.9% for females.<sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup> The country's educational system is three-tiered and heavily subsidised, with the government operating many schools at the primary, secondary and higher secondary levels and subsidising many private schools. In the tertiary education sector, the Bangladeshi government funds over 45 state universities<sup id="cite_ref-ugc-universities.gov.bd_364-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ugc-universities.gov.bd-364">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup> through the <a href="/wiki/University_Grants_Commission_(Bangladesh)" title="University Grants Commission (Bangladesh)">University Grants Commission</a> (UGC), created by Presidential Order 10 in 1973.<sup id="cite_ref-365" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-365">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The education system is divided into five levels: primary (first to fifth grade), junior secondary (sixth to eighth grade), secondary (ninth and tenth grade), higher secondary (11th and 12th grade), and tertiary.<sup id="cite_ref-CompEd_366-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CompEd-366">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup> Five years of secondary education (including junior secondary) ends with a <a href="/wiki/Secondary_School_Certificate" title="Secondary School Certificate">Secondary School Certificate</a> (SSC) examination. Since 2009, the Primary Education Closing (PEC) examination has also been introduced. Students who pass the PEC examination proceed to secondary or matriculation training, culminating in the SSC examination.<sup id="cite_ref-CompEd_366-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CompEd-366">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup> Students who pass the PEC examination proceed to three years of junior secondary education, culminating in the <a href="/wiki/Junior_School_Certificate" title="Junior School Certificate">Junior School Certificate</a> (JSC) examination. Students who pass this examination proceed to two years of secondary education, culminating in the SSC examination. Students who pass this examination proceed to two years of higher secondary education, culminating in the <a href="/wiki/Higher_Secondary_School_Certificate" title="Higher Secondary School Certificate">Higher Secondary School Certificate</a> (HSC) examination.<sup id="cite_ref-CompEd_366-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CompEd-366">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Universities_in_Bangladesh" title="Universities in Bangladesh">Universities in Bangladesh</a> are of three general types: public (government-owned and subsidised), private (privately owned universities) and international (operated and funded by international organisations). The country has 47 public,<sup id="cite_ref-ugc-universities.gov.bd_364-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ugc-universities.gov.bd-364">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup> 105 private<sup id="cite_ref-367" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-367">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> and two international <a href="/wiki/List_of_universities_in_Bangladesh" title="List of universities in Bangladesh">universities</a>; <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_National_University" class="mw-redirect" title="Bangladesh National University">Bangladesh National University</a> has the largest enrolment, and the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Dhaka" title="University of Dhaka">University of Dhaka</a> (established in 1921) is the oldest. <a href="/wiki/University_of_Chittagong" title="University of Chittagong">University of Chittagong</a>, established in 1966, has the largest campus among all universities in Bangladesh.<sup id="cite_ref-368" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-368">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup> Medical education is provided by 29 government and private <a href="/wiki/List_of_medical_colleges_in_Bangladesh" title="List of medical colleges in Bangladesh">medical colleges</a>. All medical colleges are affiliated with the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_and_Family_Welfare_(Bangladesh)" title="Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Bangladesh)">Ministry of Health and Family Welfare</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Health">Health</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Health_in_Bangladesh" title="Health in Bangladesh">Health in Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Life_expectancy_by_WBG_-Bangladesh.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Life_expectancy_by_WBG_-Bangladesh.png/220px-Life_expectancy_by_WBG_-Bangladesh.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="141" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Life_expectancy_by_WBG_-Bangladesh.png/330px-Life_expectancy_by_WBG_-Bangladesh.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Life_expectancy_by_WBG_-Bangladesh.png/440px-Life_expectancy_by_WBG_-Bangladesh.png 2x" data-file-width="1162" data-file-height="743" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Life_expectancy_by_WBG_-Bangladesh.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Historical development of <a href="/wiki/Life_expectancy" title="Life expectancy">life expectancy</a> in Bangladesh, displaying significant strides since independence.<sup id="cite_ref-369" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-369">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>Bangladesh, by constitution, guarantees healthcare services as a fundamental right to all of its citizens.<sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_and_Family_Welfare_(Bangladesh)" title="Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Bangladesh)">Ministry of Health and Family Welfare</a> is the largest institutional healthcare provider in Bangladesh,<sup id="cite_ref-overview_371-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-overview-371">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup> and contains two divisions: <a href="/wiki/Health_Service_Division" title="Health Service Division">Health Service Division</a> and <a href="/wiki/Medical_Education_And_Family_Welfare_Division" title="Medical Education And Family Welfare Division">Medical Education And Family Welfare Division</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-372" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-372">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup> However, healthcare facilities in Bangladesh are considered less than adequate, although they have improved as the economy has grown and poverty levels have decreased significantly.<sup id="cite_ref-overview_371-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-overview-371">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh faces a severe health workforce crisis, as formally-trained providers make up a short percentage the total health workforce.<sup id="cite_ref-373" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-373">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup> Significant deficiencies in the treatment practices of village doctors persist, with widespread harmful and inappropriate drug prescribing.<sup id="cite_ref-374" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-374">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup> Receiving health care from informal providers is encouraged.<sup id="cite_ref-375" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-375">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh's poor healthcare system suffers from severe underfunding from the government.<sup id="cite_ref-overview_371-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-overview-371">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup> As of 2019<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bangladesh&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, some 2.48% of total GDP was attributed to healthcare,<sup id="cite_ref-376" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-376">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup> and domestic general government spending on healthcare was 18.63% of the total budget,<sup id="cite_ref-377" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-377">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> while out-of-pocket expenditures made up the vast majority of total budget, totalling 72.68%.<sup id="cite_ref-378" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-378">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup> Domestic private health expenditure was about 75% of the total healthcare expenditure.<sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup> As of 2020<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bangladesh&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, there are only 5.3 doctors per 10,000 people, and about 6 physicians<sup id="cite_ref-380" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-380">&#91;380&#93;</a></sup> and 3 nurses per 10,000 people, while the number of hospital beds is 8 per 10,000.<sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381">&#91;381&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-382" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-382">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup> The overall life expectancy in Bangladesh at birth was 73 years (71 years for males and 75 years for females) as of 2020<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bangladesh&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>,<sup id="cite_ref-383" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-383">&#91;383&#93;</a></sup> and it has a comparably high <a href="/wiki/Infant_mortality" title="Infant mortality">infant mortality</a> rate (24 per 1,000 live births) and <a href="/wiki/Child_mortality" title="Child mortality">child mortality</a> rate (29 per 1,000 live births).<sup id="cite_ref-384" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-384">&#91;384&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-385" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-385">&#91;385&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Maternal_death" title="Maternal death">Maternal mortality</a> remains high, clocking at 173 per 100,000 live births.<sup id="cite_ref-386" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-386">&#91;386&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh is a key source market for <a href="/wiki/Medical_tourism" title="Medical tourism">medical tourism</a> for various countries, mainly <a href="/wiki/Medical_tourism_in_India" title="Medical tourism in India">India</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-387" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-387">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup> due to its citizens dissatisfaction and distrust over their own healthcare system.<sup id="cite_ref-388" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-388">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The main causes of death are <a href="/wiki/Coronary_artery_disease" title="Coronary artery disease">coronary artery disease</a>, <a href="/wiki/Stroke" title="Stroke">stroke</a>, and chronic <a href="/wiki/Respiratory_disease" title="Respiratory disease">respiratory disease</a>; comprising 62% and 60% of all adult male and female deaths, respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-389" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-389">&#91;389&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Malnutrition" title="Malnutrition">Malnutrition</a> is a major and persistent problem in Bangladesh, mainly affecting the rural regions, more than half of the population suffers from it. Severe acute malnutrition affects 450,000 children, while close to 2 million children have moderate acute malnutrition. For children under the age of five, 52% are affected by <a href="/wiki/Anaemia" class="mw-redirect" title="Anaemia">anaemia</a>, 41% are <a href="/wiki/Stunted_growth" title="Stunted growth">stunted</a>, 16% are <a href="/wiki/Wasting" title="Wasting">wasted</a>, and 36% are <a href="/wiki/Underweight" title="Underweight">underweight</a>. A quarter of women are underweight and around 15% have short stature, while over half also suffer from anaemia.<sup id="cite_ref-390" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-390">&#91;390&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Culture">Culture</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Bangladesh" title="Culture of Bangladesh">Culture of Bangladesh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Bengal" title="Culture of Bengal">Culture of Bengal</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Bengali_Renaissance" title="Bengali Renaissance">Bengali Renaissance</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Visual_arts_and_crafts">Visual arts and crafts</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Bangladeshi_art" title="Bangladeshi art">Bangladeshi art</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:A_10_feet_high_ancient_bed_in_National_Museum_of_Bangladesh_collected_from_Lohagara,Narail.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/A_10_feet_high_ancient_bed_in_National_Museum_of_Bangladesh_collected_from_Lohagara%2CNarail.jpg/220px-A_10_feet_high_ancient_bed_in_National_Museum_of_Bangladesh_collected_from_Lohagara%2CNarail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/A_10_feet_high_ancient_bed_in_National_Museum_of_Bangladesh_collected_from_Lohagara%2CNarail.jpg/330px-A_10_feet_high_ancient_bed_in_National_Museum_of_Bangladesh_collected_from_Lohagara%2CNarail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/A_10_feet_high_ancient_bed_in_National_Museum_of_Bangladesh_collected_from_Lohagara%2CNarail.jpg/440px-A_10_feet_high_ancient_bed_in_National_Museum_of_Bangladesh_collected_from_Lohagara%2CNarail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="3000" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:A_10_feet_high_ancient_bed_in_National_Museum_of_Bangladesh_collected_from_Lohagara,Narail.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Furniture (beds) belonging the historic <a href="/wiki/Zamindars_of_Bengal" title="Zamindars of Bengal">Zamindars of Bengal</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_National_Museum" title="Bangladesh National Museum">Bangladesh National Museum</a></div></div></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Kantha_(Quilt)_LACMA_AC1994.131.1.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Kantha_%28Quilt%29_LACMA_AC1994.131.1.jpg/220px-Kantha_%28Quilt%29_LACMA_AC1994.131.1.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="162" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Kantha_%28Quilt%29_LACMA_AC1994.131.1.jpg/330px-Kantha_%28Quilt%29_LACMA_AC1994.131.1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Kantha_%28Quilt%29_LACMA_AC1994.131.1.jpg/440px-Kantha_%28Quilt%29_LACMA_AC1994.131.1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2100" data-file-height="1548" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Kantha_(Quilt)_LACMA_AC1994.131.1.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Embroidery on <a href="/wiki/Nakshi_kantha" title="Nakshi kantha">Nakshi kantha</a> (embroidered <a href="/wiki/Quilt" title="Quilt">quilt</a>), a centuries-old Bengali art tradition</div></div></div>
<p>The recorded history of art in Bangladesh can be traced to the 3rd century BCE, when <a href="/wiki/Terracotta" title="Terracotta">terracotta</a> sculptures were made in the region. In classical antiquity, a notable sculptural Hindu, Jain and Buddhist art developed in the Pala Empire and the Sena dynasty. Islamic art has evolved since the 14th century. The architecture of the Bengal Sultanate saw a distinct style of domed mosques with complex niche pillars that had no minarets. <a href="/wiki/Mughal_Bengal" class="mw-redirect" title="Mughal Bengal">Mughal Bengal</a>'s most celebrated artistic tradition was the weaving of <a href="/wiki/Jamdani" title="Jamdani">Jamdani</a> <a href="/wiki/Motif_(textile_arts)" title="Motif (textile arts)">motifs</a> on fine muslin, which is now classified by UNESCO as an <a href="/wiki/Intangible_cultural_heritage" title="Intangible cultural heritage">intangible cultural heritage</a>. Jamdani motifs were similar to Iranian textile art (buta motifs) and Western textile art (<a href="/wiki/Paisley_(design)" title="Paisley (design)">paisley</a>). The Jamdani weavers in Dhaka received imperial patronage.<sup id="cite_ref-star_79-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-star-79">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-391" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-391">&#91;391&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Ivory" title="Ivory">Ivory</a> and <a href="/wiki/Brass" title="Brass">brass</a> were also widely used in Mughal art. <a href="/wiki/Pottery" title="Pottery">Pottery</a> is widely used in Bengali culture.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Modern_art" title="Modern art">modern art</a> movement in Bangladesh took shape during the 1950s, particularly with the pioneering works of <a href="/wiki/Zainul_Abedin" title="Zainul Abedin">Zainul Abedin</a>. East Bengal developed its own modernist painting and sculpture traditions, which were distinct from the art movements in West Bengal. The <a href="/wiki/Art_Institute_Dhaka" class="mw-redirect" title="Art Institute Dhaka">Art Institute Dhaka</a> has been an important centre for visual art in the region. Its annual <a href="/wiki/Mangal_Shobhajatra" title="Mangal Shobhajatra">Bengali New Year parade</a> was enlisted as an intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO in 2016.
</p><p>Modern Bangladesh has produced many of South Asia's leading painters, including <a href="/wiki/SM_Sultan" title="SM Sultan">SM Sultan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mohammad_Kibria" title="Mohammad Kibria">Mohammad Kibria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shahabuddin_Ahmed_(artist)" title="Shahabuddin Ahmed (artist)">Shahabuddin Ahmed</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kanak_Chanpa_Chakma" title="Kanak Chanpa Chakma">Kanak Chanpa Chakma</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kafil_Ahmed" title="Kafil Ahmed">Kafil Ahmed</a>, <a href="/wiki/Saifuddin_Ahmed" title="Saifuddin Ahmed">Saifuddin Ahmed</a>, <a href="/wiki/Qayyum_Chowdhury" title="Qayyum Chowdhury">Qayyum Chowdhury</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rashid_Choudhury" title="Rashid Choudhury">Rashid Choudhury</a>, <a href="/wiki/Quamrul_Hassan" title="Quamrul Hassan">Quamrul Hassan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rafiqun_Nabi" title="Rafiqun Nabi">Rafiqun Nabi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Syed_Jahangir" title="Syed Jahangir">Syed Jahangir</a>, among others. <a href="/wiki/Novera_Ahmed" title="Novera Ahmed">Novera Ahmed</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nitun_Kundu" title="Nitun Kundu">Nitun Kundu</a> were the country's pioneers of modernist sculpture.
</p><p>In recent times, photography as a medium of art has become popular. Biennial <a href="/wiki/Chobi_Mela" class="mw-redirect" title="Chobi Mela">Chobi Mela</a> is considered the largest photography festival in Asia.<sup id="cite_ref-392" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-392">&#91;392&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Literature">Literature</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Bangladeshi_literature" class="mw-redirect" title="Bangladeshi literature">Bangladeshi literature</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Syed_Mujtaba_Ali.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Syed_Mujtaba_Ali.jpg/220px-Syed_Mujtaba_Ali.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="231" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/29/Syed_Mujtaba_Ali.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="250" data-file-height="263" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Syed_Mujtaba_Ali.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Syed_Mujtaba_Ali" title="Syed Mujtaba Ali">Syed Mujtaba Ali</a></div></div></div>
<p>The oldest evidence of writing in Bangladesh is the Mahasthan <a href="/wiki/Brahmi" class="mw-redirect" title="Brahmi">Brahmi</a> Inscription, which dates back to the 3rd century BCE.<sup id="cite_ref-393" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-393">&#91;393&#93;</a></sup> In the Gupta Empire, Sanskrit literature thrived in the region. Bengali developed from <a href="/wiki/Sanskrit" title="Sanskrit">Sanskrit</a> and <a href="/wiki/Magadhi_Prakrit" title="Magadhi Prakrit">Magadhi Prakrit</a> in the 8th to 10th century. Bengali literature is a millennium-old tradition; the <a href="/wiki/Charyapada" title="Charyapada">Charyapadas</a> are the earliest examples of Bengali poetry. Sufi spiritualism inspired many <a href="/wiki/Bengali_Muslim" class="mw-redirect" title="Bengali Muslim">Bengali Muslim</a> writers. During the Bengal Sultanate, medieval Bengali writers were influenced by <a href="/wiki/Arabic_literature" title="Arabic literature">Arabic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Persian_literature" title="Persian literature">Persian works</a>. Sultans of Bengal patronized Bengali literature. Examples include the writings of <a href="/wiki/Maladhar_Basu" title="Maladhar Basu">Maladhar Basu</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bipradas_Pipilai" title="Bipradas Pipilai">Bipradas Pipilai</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vijay_Gupta_(poet)" title="Vijay Gupta (poet)">Vijay Gupta</a> and Yasoraj Khan. The <a href="/wiki/Chandidas" title="Chandidas">Chandidas</a> are the notable lyric poets from the early Medieval Age. <a href="/wiki/Alaol" title="Alaol">Syed Alaol</a> was the bard of middle Bengali literature. The Bengal Renaissance shaped modern Bengali literature, including novels, short stories and <a href="/wiki/Bengali_science_fiction" title="Bengali science fiction">science fiction</a>. Rabindranath Tagore was the first non-European laureate of the <a href="/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature" title="Nobel Prize in Literature">Nobel Prize in Literature</a> and is described as the Bengali Shakespeare.<sup id="cite_ref-394" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-394">&#91;394&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Kazi_Nazrul_Islam" title="Kazi Nazrul Islam">Kazi Nazrul Islam</a> was a revolutionary poet who espoused political rebellion against colonialism and fascism. <a href="/wiki/Begum_Rokeya" title="Begum Rokeya">Begum Rokeya</a> is regarded as the pioneer feminist writer of Bangladesh.<sup id="cite_ref-Rubaiyat_395-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Rubaiyat-395">&#91;395&#93;</a></sup> Other renaissance icons included Michael Madhusudan Dutt and <a href="/wiki/Sarat_Chandra_Chattopadhyay" title="Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay">Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay</a>.
The writer <a href="/wiki/Syed_Mujtaba_Ali" title="Syed Mujtaba Ali">Syed Mujtaba Ali</a> is noted for his cosmopolitan Bengali worldview.<sup id="cite_ref-396" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-396">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Jasimuddin" title="Jasimuddin">Jasimuddin</a> was a renowned pastoral poet. <a href="/wiki/Shamsur_Rahman_(poet)" title="Shamsur Rahman (poet)">Shamsur Rahman</a> and <a href="/wiki/Al_Mahmud" title="Al Mahmud">Al Mahmud</a> are considered two of the greatest Bengali poets to have emerged in the 20th century. <a href="/wiki/Farrukh_Ahmad" title="Farrukh Ahmad">Farrukh Ahmad</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sufia_Kamal" title="Sufia Kamal">Sufia Kamal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Syed_Ali_Ahsan" title="Syed Ali Ahsan">Syed Ali Ahsan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ahsan_Habib" title="Ahsan Habib">Ahsan Habib</a>, <a href="/wiki/Abul_Hussain" title="Abul Hussain">Abul Hussain</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shahid_Qadri" title="Shahid Qadri">Shahid Qadri</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fazal_Shahabuddin" title="Fazal Shahabuddin">Fazal Shahabuddin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Abu_Zafar_Obaidullah" title="Abu Zafar Obaidullah">Abu Zafar Obaidullah</a>, <a href="/wiki/Omar_Ali_(poet)" title="Omar Ali (poet)">Omar Ali</a>, <a href="/wiki/Al_Mujahidi" title="Al Mujahidi">Al Mujahidi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Syed_Shamsul_Huq" class="mw-redirect" title="Syed Shamsul Huq">Syed Shamsul Huq</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nirmalendu_Goon" title="Nirmalendu Goon">Nirmalendu Goon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Abid_Azad" title="Abid Azad">Abid Azad</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hasan_Hafizur_Rahman" title="Hasan Hafizur Rahman">Hasan Hafizur Rahman</a> and <a href="/wiki/Abdul_Hye_Sikder" title="Abdul Hye Sikder">Abdul Hye Sikder</a> are important figures of modern Bangladeshi poetry. <a href="/wiki/Ahmed_Sofa" title="Ahmed Sofa">Ahmed Sofa</a> is regarded as the most important Bangladeshi intellectual in the post-independence era. <a href="/wiki/Humayun_Ahmed" title="Humayun Ahmed">Humayun Ahmed</a> was a popular writer of modern Bangladeshi <a href="/wiki/Magical_realism" class="mw-redirect" title="Magical realism">magical realism</a> and science fiction. Notable writers of Bangladeshi fictions include Mir Mosharraf Hossain, <a href="/wiki/Akhteruzzaman_Elias" title="Akhteruzzaman Elias">Akhteruzzaman Elias</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alauddin_Al_Azad" class="mw-redirect" title="Alauddin Al Azad">Alauddin Al Azad</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shahidul_Zahir" title="Shahidul Zahir">Shahidul Zahir</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rashid_Karim" title="Rashid Karim">Rashid Karim</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mahmudul_Haque" title="Mahmudul Haque">Mahmudul Haque</a>, <a href="/wiki/Syed_Waliullah" title="Syed Waliullah">Syed Waliullah</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shahidullah_Kaiser" title="Shahidullah Kaiser">Shahidullah Kaiser</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shawkat_Osman" title="Shawkat Osman">Shawkat Osman</a>, <a href="/wiki/Selina_Hossain" title="Selina Hossain">Selina Hossain</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shahed_Ali" title="Shahed Ali">Shahed Ali</a>, <a href="/wiki/Razia_Khan" title="Razia Khan">Razia Khan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Anisul_Hoque" title="Anisul Hoque">Anisul Hoque</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Abdul_Mannan_Syed" title="Abdul Mannan Syed">Abdul Mannan Syed</a>.
</p><p>The annual <a href="/wiki/Ekushey_Book_Fair" title="Ekushey Book Fair">Ekushey Book Fair</a> and <a href="/wiki/Hay_Festival_Dhaka" class="mw-redirect" title="Hay Festival Dhaka">Dhaka Literature Festival</a>, organised by the <a href="/wiki/Bangla_Academy" title="Bangla Academy">Bangla Academy</a>, are among the largest literary festivals in South Asia.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Women">Women</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Women_in_Bangladesh" title="Women in Bangladesh">Women in Bangladesh</a></div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Gender_inequality_in_Bangladesh" title="Gender inequality in Bangladesh">Gender inequality in Bangladesh</a></div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Child_marriage_in_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Child marriage in Bangladesh">Child marriage in Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:BegumRokeyaWithHusband.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/BegumRokeyaWithHusband.jpg/220px-BegumRokeyaWithHusband.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="268" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/BegumRokeyaWithHusband.jpg/330px-BegumRokeyaWithHusband.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b0/BegumRokeyaWithHusband.jpg 2x" data-file-width="420" data-file-height="512" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:BegumRokeyaWithHusband.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Muslim feminist <a href="/wiki/Begum_Rokeya" title="Begum Rokeya">Begum Rokeya</a> and her husband in 1898</div></div></div>
<p>Although as of 2015<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bangladesh&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, several women occupied major political office in Bangladesh. Its women continue to live under a patriarchal social regime where violence is common.<sup id="cite_ref-whispers_397-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-whispers-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> Whereas in India and Pakistan women participate less in the workforce as their education increases, the reverse is the case in Bangladesh.<sup id="cite_ref-whispers_397-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-whispers-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bengal has a long history of <a href="/wiki/Feminist_activism" class="mw-redirect" title="Feminist activism">feminist activism</a> dating back to the 19th century. <a href="/wiki/Begum_Rokeya" title="Begum Rokeya">Begum Rokeya</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nawab_Faizunnesa" title="Nawab Faizunnesa">Faizunnessa Chowdhurani</a> played an important role in emancipating Bengali Muslim women from <a href="/wiki/Purdah" title="Purdah">purdah</a>, before the country's division, as well as promoting girls' education. Several women were elected to the Bengal Legislative Assembly in the British Raj. The first women's magazine, <i><a href="/wiki/Begum_(magazine)" title="Begum (magazine)">Begum</a></i>, was published in 1948.
</p><p>In 2008, Bangladeshi female workforce participation stood at 26%.<sup id="cite_ref-398" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-398">&#91;398&#93;</a></sup> Women dominate <a href="/wiki/Blue_collar" class="mw-redirect" title="Blue collar">blue collar</a> jobs in the Bangladeshi garment industry. Agriculture, social services, healthcare and education are also major occupations for Bangladeshi women, while their employment in <a href="/wiki/White-collar_worker" title="White-collar worker">white collar</a> positions has steadily increased.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Architecture">Architecture</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Architecture_of_Bangladesh" title="Architecture of Bangladesh">Architecture of Bangladesh</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:592px;max-width:592px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:242px;max-width:242px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Mosque_in_the_15th_century_Bengal_style.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Mosque_in_the_15th_century_Bengal_style.jpg/240px-Mosque_in_the_15th_century_Bengal_style.jpg" decoding="async"
