//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Mosque_in_the_15th_century_Bengal_style.jpg/480px-Mosque_in_the_15th_century_Bengal_style.jpg 2x" data-file-width="735" data-file-height="528" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">Mosque in the 15th century <a href="/wiki/Bengal_Sultanate" title="Bengal Sultanate">Bengal style</a></div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Zoffany-Lalbagh_Fort.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Zoffany-Lalbagh_Fort.jpg/200px-Zoffany-Lalbagh_Fort.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="171" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Zoffany-Lalbagh_Fort.jpg/300px-Zoffany-Lalbagh_Fort.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Zoffany-Lalbagh_Fort.jpg/400px-Zoffany-Lalbagh_Fort.jpg 2x" data-file-width="900" data-file-height="770" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">'The South Gate of the <a href="/wiki/Lalbagh_Fort" title="Lalbagh Fort">Lalbagh Fort</a>' by <a href="/wiki/Johan_Zoffany" title="Johan Zoffany">Johan Zoffany</a></div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:142px;max-width:142px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Kantaji_Temple_1870%27s.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Kantaji_Temple_1870%27s.jpg/140px-Kantaji_Temple_1870%27s.jpg" decoding="async" width="140" height="172" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Kantaji_Temple_1870%27s.jpg/210px-Kantaji_Temple_1870%27s.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Kantaji_Temple_1870%27s.jpg/280px-Kantaji_Temple_1870%27s.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3249" data-file-height="4000" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">18th century <a href="/wiki/Terracotta" title="Terracotta">terracotta</a> <a href="/wiki/Kantanagar_Temple" class="mw-redirect" title="Kantanagar Temple">Kantanagar Temple</a></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>The architectural traditions of Bangladesh have a 2,500-year-old heritage.<sup id="cite_ref-399" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-399">&#91;399&#93;</a></sup> Terracotta architecture is a distinct feature of Bengal. Pre-Islamic Bengali architecture reached its pinnacle in the Pala Empire, when the Pala School of Sculptural Art established grand structures such as the Somapura Mahavihara. <a href="/wiki/Islamic_architecture" title="Islamic architecture">Islamic architecture</a> began developing under the Bengal Sultanate, when local terracotta styles influenced medieval mosque construction.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Sixty_Dome_Mosque" title="Sixty Dome Mosque">Sixty Dome Mosque</a> was the largest medieval mosque built in Bangladesh and is a fine example of Turkic-Bengali architecture. The <a href="/wiki/Mughal_architecture" title="Mughal architecture">Mughal style</a> replaced indigenous architecture when Bengal became a province of the Mughal Empire and influenced urban housing development. The <a href="/wiki/Kantajew_Temple" title="Kantajew Temple">Kantajew Temple</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dhakeshwari_Temple" title="Dhakeshwari Temple">Dhakeshwari Temple</a> are excellent examples of late medieval <a href="/wiki/Hindu_temple_architecture" title="Hindu temple architecture">Hindu temple architecture</a>. <a href="/wiki/Indo-Saracenic_Revival_architecture" class="mw-redirect" title="Indo-Saracenic Revival architecture">Indo-Saracenic Revival architecture</a>, based on Indo-Islamic styles, flourished during the British period. The zamindar gentry in Bangladesh built numerous Indo-Saracenic palaces and country mansions, such as the <a href="/wiki/Ahsan_Manzil" title="Ahsan Manzil">Ahsan Manzil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tajhat_Palace" title="Tajhat Palace">Tajhat Palace</a>, <a href="/wiki/Uttara_Gonobhaban" class="mw-redirect" title="Uttara Gonobhaban">Dighapatia Palace</a>, <a href="/wiki/Puthia_Rajbari" title="Puthia Rajbari">Puthia Rajbari</a> and <a href="/wiki/Natore_Rajbari" title="Natore Rajbari">Natore Rajbari</a>.
</p><p>Bengali <a href="/wiki/Vernacular_architecture" title="Vernacular architecture">vernacular architecture</a> is noted for pioneering the <a href="/wiki/Bungalow" title="Bungalow">bungalow</a>. Bangladeshi villages consist of <a href="/wiki/Thatch" class="mw-redirect" title="Thatch">thatched</a> roofed houses made of natural materials like <a href="/wiki/Mud" title="Mud">mud</a>, <a href="/wiki/Straw" title="Straw">straw</a>, wood and bamboo. In modern times, village bungalows are increasingly made of <a href="/wiki/Tin" title="Tin">tin</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Muzharul_Islam" title="Muzharul Islam">Muzharul Islam</a> was the pioneer of Bangladeshi modern architecture. His varied works set the course of modern architectural practice in the country. Islam brought leading global architects, including <a href="/wiki/Louis_Kahn" title="Louis Kahn">Louis Kahn</a>, <a href="/wiki/Richard_Neutra" title="Richard Neutra">Richard Neutra</a>, <a href="/wiki/Stanley_Tigerman" title="Stanley Tigerman">Stanley Tigerman</a>, <a href="/wiki/Paul_Rudolph_(architect)" title="Paul Rudolph (architect)">Paul Rudolph</a>, <a href="/wiki/Robert_Boughey" title="Robert Boughey">Robert Boughey</a> and <a href="/wiki/Konstantinos_Apostolos_Doxiadis" class="mw-redirect" title="Konstantinos Apostolos Doxiadis">Konstantinos Doxiadis</a>, to work in erstwhile East Pakistan. Louis Kahn was chosen to design the National Parliament Complex in <a href="/wiki/Sher-e-Bangla_Nagar" title="Sher-e-Bangla Nagar">Sher-e-Bangla Nagar</a>. Kahn's monumental designs, combining regional red brick aesthetics, his own concrete and marble <a href="/wiki/Brutalism" class="mw-redirect" title="Brutalism">brutalism</a> and the use of lakes to represent Bengali geography, are regarded as one of the masterpieces of the 20th century. In more recent times, award-winning architects like <a href="/wiki/Rafiq_Azam" title="Rafiq Azam">Rafiq Azam</a> have set the course of contemporary architecture by adopting influences from the works of Islam and Kahn.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Performing_arts">Performing arts</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Culture_of_Bangladesh.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Culture_of_Bangladesh.jpg/220px-Culture_of_Bangladesh.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Culture_of_Bangladesh.jpg/330px-Culture_of_Bangladesh.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Culture_of_Bangladesh.jpg/440px-Culture_of_Bangladesh.jpg 2x" data-file-width="900" data-file-height="600" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Culture_of_Bangladesh.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>A tribal <a href="/wiki/Manipuri_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Manipuri people">Manipuri</a> dancer from <a href="/wiki/Sylhet_Division" title="Sylhet Division">Sylhet</a></div></div></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladesh_Udichi_Shilpigoshthi_-_Chittagong_University_Sangsad_celebrating_Pohela_Falgun_1423_at_CU_Muktomoncho_(02).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Bangladesh_Udichi_Shilpigoshthi_-_Chittagong_University_Sangsad_celebrating_Pohela_Falgun_1423_at_CU_Muktomoncho_%2802%29.jpg/220px-Bangladesh_Udichi_Shilpigoshthi_-_Chittagong_University_Sangsad_celebrating_Pohela_Falgun_1423_at_CU_Muktomoncho_%2802%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Bangladesh_Udichi_Shilpigoshthi_-_Chittagong_University_Sangsad_celebrating_Pohela_Falgun_1423_at_CU_Muktomoncho_%2802%29.jpg/330px-Bangladesh_Udichi_Shilpigoshthi_-_Chittagong_University_Sangsad_celebrating_Pohela_Falgun_1423_at_CU_Muktomoncho_%2802%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Bangladesh_Udichi_Shilpigoshthi_-_Chittagong_University_Sangsad_celebrating_Pohela_Falgun_1423_at_CU_Muktomoncho_%2802%29.jpg/440px-Bangladesh_Udichi_Shilpigoshthi_-_Chittagong_University_Sangsad_celebrating_Pohela_Falgun_1423_at_CU_Muktomoncho_%2802%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5184" data-file-height="3456" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladesh_Udichi_Shilpigoshthi_-_Chittagong_University_Sangsad_celebrating_Pohela_Falgun_1423_at_CU_Muktomoncho_(02).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Women dancers during the <a href="/wiki/Bengali_New_Year" class="mw-redirect" title="Bengali New Year">Bengali New Year</a> in Chittagong</div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Theatre_in_Bangladesh" title="Theatre in Bangladesh">Theatre in Bangladesh</a> includes various forms with a history dating back to the 4th century CE.<sup id="cite_ref-Ahmed,_Syed_Jamil_2000_p._396_400-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ahmed,_Syed_Jamil_2000_p._396-400">&#91;400&#93;</a></sup> It includes narrative forms, song and dance forms, supra-personae forms, performances with scroll paintings, puppet theatre and processional forms.<sup id="cite_ref-Ahmed,_Syed_Jamil_2000_p._396_400-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ahmed,_Syed_Jamil_2000_p._396-400">&#91;400&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Jatra_(theatre)" title="Jatra (theatre)">Jatra</a> is the most popular form of Bengali folk theatre.
The dance traditions of Bangladesh include indigenous tribal and Bengali dance forms, as well as <a href="/wiki/Classical_Indian_dance" class="mw-redirect" title="Classical Indian dance">classical Indian dances</a>, including the <a href="/wiki/Kathak" title="Kathak">Kathak</a>, <a href="/wiki/Odissi" title="Odissi">Odissi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Manipuri_dance" class="mw-redirect" title="Manipuri dance">Manipuri dances</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Music_of_Bangladesh" title="Music of Bangladesh">music of Bangladesh</a> features the <a href="/wiki/Baul" title="Baul">Baul</a> <a href="/wiki/Mysticism" title="Mysticism">mystical</a> tradition, listed by UNESCO as a <a href="/wiki/Masterpiece_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity" class="mw-redirect" title="Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity">Masterpiece of Intangible Cultural Heritage</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-401" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-401">&#91;401&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Lalon" title="Lalon">Fakir Lalon Shah</a> popularised <a href="/wiki/Baul" title="Baul">Baul</a> music in the country in the 18th century and it has since been one of the most popular music genera in the country since then. Most modern <a href="/wiki/Bauls" class="mw-redirect" title="Bauls">Bauls</a> are devoted to Lalon Shah.<sup id="cite_ref-402" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-402">&#91;402&#93;</a></sup> Numerous lyric-based musical traditions, varying from one region to the next, exist, including <a href="/wiki/Gombhira" title="Gombhira">Gombhira</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bhatiali" title="Bhatiali">Bhatiali</a> and <a href="/wiki/Bhawaiya" title="Bhawaiya">Bhawaiya</a>. Folk music is accompanied by a one-stringed instrument known as the <a href="/wiki/Ektara" title="Ektara">ektara</a>. Other instruments include the <a href="/wiki/Dotara" title="Dotara">dotara</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dhol" title="Dhol">dhol</a>, flute, and <a href="/wiki/Tabla" title="Tabla">tabla</a>. Bengali classical music includes <a href="/wiki/Tagore_songs" class="mw-redirect" title="Tagore songs">Tagore songs</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nazrul_geeti" class="mw-redirect" title="Nazrul geeti">Nazrul Sangeet</a>. Bangladesh has a rich tradition of <a href="/wiki/Indian_classical_music" title="Indian classical music">Indian classical music</a>, which uses instruments like the <a href="/wiki/Sitar" title="Sitar">sitar</a>, tabla, <a href="/wiki/Sarod" title="Sarod">sarod</a> and <a href="/wiki/Santoor" title="Santoor">santoor</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-403" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Sabina_Yasmin" title="Sabina Yasmin">Sabina Yasmin</a> and <a href="/wiki/Runa_Laila" title="Runa Laila">Runa Laila</a> are considered the leading playback singers in the modern time, while musicians such as <a href="/wiki/Ayub_Bachchu" title="Ayub Bachchu">Ayub Bachchu</a> and <a href="/wiki/James_(musician)" title="James (musician)">James</a> are credited with popularising rock music in Bangladesh.<sup id="cite_ref-404" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-404">&#91;404&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-405" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-405">&#91;405&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Textiles">Textiles</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Textile_arts_of_Bangladesh" title="Textile arts of Bangladesh">Textile arts of Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Muslin_trade_in_Bengal" title="Muslin trade in Bengal">Muslin trade in Bengal</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Fashion_Exhibition_of_Bangladesh.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Fashion_Exhibition_of_Bangladesh.jpg/220px-Fashion_Exhibition_of_Bangladesh.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="330" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Fashion_Exhibition_of_Bangladesh.jpg/330px-Fashion_Exhibition_of_Bangladesh.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Fashion_Exhibition_of_Bangladesh.jpg/440px-Fashion_Exhibition_of_Bangladesh.jpg 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="1200" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Fashion_Exhibition_of_Bangladesh.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>A ramp walk by a model during a fashion show in Bangladesh in 2012</div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Nakshi_Kantha" class="mw-redirect" title="Nakshi Kantha">Nakshi Kantha</a> is a centuries-old <a href="/wiki/Embroidery" title="Embroidery">embroidery</a> tradition for <a href="/wiki/Quilt" title="Quilt">quilts</a>, said to be indigenous to eastern Bengal (i.e. Bangladesh). The sari is the national dress for Bangladeshi women. Mughal Dhaka was renowned for producing the finest <a href="/wiki/Muslin" title="Muslin">Muslin</a> saris, as well as the famed <a href="/wiki/Dhakai" title="Dhakai">Dhakai</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jamdani" title="Jamdani">Jamdani</a>, the weaving of which is listed by UNESCO as one of the masterpieces of humanity's intangible cultural heritage.<sup id="cite_ref-406" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-406">&#91;406&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh also produces the <a href="/wiki/Rajshahi_silk" title="Rajshahi silk">Rajshahi silk</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Shalwar_kameez" title="Shalwar kameez">shalwar kameez</a> is also widely worn by Bangladeshi women. In urban areas, some women can be seen in western clothing. The <a href="/wiki/Kurta" title="Kurta">kurta</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sherwani" title="Sherwani">sherwani</a> are the national dress of Bangladeshi men; the <a href="/wiki/Lungi" title="Lungi">lungi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dhoti" title="Dhoti">dhoti</a> are worn by them in informal settings. Aside from ethnic wear, domestically <a href="/wiki/Tailored" class="mw-redirect" title="Tailored">tailored</a> <a href="/wiki/Suit_(clothing)" class="mw-redirect" title="Suit (clothing)">suits</a> and <a href="/wiki/Neckties" class="mw-redirect" title="Neckties">neckties</a> are customarily worn by the country's men in offices, in schools and at social events.
</p><p>The handloom industry supplies 60–65% of the country's clothing demand.<sup id="cite_ref-407" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-407">&#91;407&#93;</a></sup> The Bengali ethnic <a href="/wiki/Fashion_industry" class="mw-redirect" title="Fashion industry">fashion industry</a> has flourished in the changing environment of the fashion world. The retailer <a href="/wiki/Aarong" title="Aarong">Aarong</a> is one of South Asia's most successful ethnic wear brands. The development of the Bangladesh textile industry, which supplies leading international brands, has promoted the local production and retail of modern Western attire. The country now has a number of expanding local brands like Westecs and Yellow. Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garments exporter. Among Bangladesh's fashion designers, <a href="/wiki/Bibi_Russell" title="Bibi Russell">Bibi Russell</a> has received international acclaim for her "Fashion for Development" shows.<sup id="cite_ref-408" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-408">&#91;408&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cuisine">Cuisine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Bangladeshi_cuisine" title="Bangladeshi cuisine">Bangladeshi cuisine</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Bengali_cuisine" title="Bengali cuisine">Bengali cuisine</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladeshi_cuisine.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Bangladeshi_cuisine.png/220px-Bangladeshi_cuisine.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="177" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Bangladeshi_cuisine.png/330px-Bangladeshi_cuisine.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Bangladeshi_cuisine.png/440px-Bangladeshi_cuisine.png 2x" data-file-width="1608" data-file-height="1296" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Bangladeshi_cuisine.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Traditional Bangladeshi meals: <a href="/wiki/Shorshe_ilish" title="Shorshe ilish">shorshe ilish</a>, Dhakaiya <a href="/wiki/Biryani" title="Biryani">biryani</a> and <a href="/wiki/Pitha" title="Pitha">pitha</a></div></div></div>
<p>Bangladeshi cuisine, formed by its geographic location and climate, is rich and varied; sharing its culinary heritage with the neighbouring Indian state of <a href="/wiki/West_Bengal" title="West Bengal">West Bengal</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cuisine_409-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cuisine-409">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 14">&#58;&#8202;14&#8202;</span></sup> <a href="/wiki/White_rice" title="White rice">White rice</a> is the staple, and along with <a href="/wiki/Fish" title="Fish">fish</a>, forms the culinary base. Varieties of <a href="/wiki/Leaf_vegetable" title="Leaf vegetable">leaf vegetables</a>, <a href="/wiki/Potato" title="Potato">potatoes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gourd" title="Gourd">gourds</a> and <a href="/wiki/Lentil" title="Lentil">lentils</a> (<a href="/wiki/Dal" title="Dal">dal</a>) also play an important role. <a href="/wiki/Curry" title="Curry">Curries</a> of <a href="/wiki/Beef" title="Beef">beef</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mutton" class="mw-redirect" title="Mutton">mutton</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chicken" title="Chicken">chicken</a> and <a href="/wiki/Duck" title="Duck">duck</a> are commonly consumed,<sup id="cite_ref-shaheda_410-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shaheda-410">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup> along with multiple types of <a href="/wiki/Bhurta" title="Bhurta">bhortas</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-411" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-411">&#91;411&#93;</a></sup> <i>bhajis</i> and <i>torkaris</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-cuisine_409-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cuisine-409">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 8">&#58;&#8202;8&#8202;</span></sup> Mughal-influenced dishes include <a href="/wiki/Korma" title="Korma">kormas</a>, kalias, <a href="/wiki/Biryani" title="Biryani">biryanis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pilaf" title="Pilaf">pulaos</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tahri_(dish)" title="Tahri (dish)">teharis</a> and <a href="/wiki/Khichuri" class="mw-redirect" title="Khichuri">khichuris</a>. Among the various spices, <a href="/wiki/Turmeric" title="Turmeric">turmeric</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fenugreek" title="Fenugreek">fenugreek</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nigella" title="Nigella">nigella</a>, <a href="/wiki/Coriander" title="Coriander">coriander</a>, <a href="/wiki/Anise" title="Anise">anise</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cardamom" title="Cardamom">cardamom</a> and <a href="/wiki/Chili_powder" title="Chili powder">chili powder</a> are widely used; a famous spice mix is the <a href="/wiki/Panch_phoron" title="Panch phoron">panch phoron</a>. Among the condiments and herbs used, <a href="/wiki/Red_onion" title="Red onion">red onions</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chili_pepper" title="Chili pepper">green chillies</a>, <a href="/wiki/Garlic" title="Garlic">garlic</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ginger" title="Ginger">ginger</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cilantro" class="mw-redirect" title="Cilantro">cilantro</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Mentha" title="Mentha">mint</a> stand out.<sup id="cite_ref-cuisine_409-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cuisine-409">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 12">&#58;&#8202;12&#8202;</span></sup> <a href="/wiki/Coconut_milk" title="Coconut milk">Coconut milk</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mustard_(condiment)" title="Mustard (condiment)">mustard paste</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mustard_seeds" class="mw-redirect" title="Mustard seeds">mustard seeds</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mustard_oil" title="Mustard oil">mustard oil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ghee" title="Ghee">ghee</a>, <a href="/wiki/South_Asian_pickle" title="South Asian pickle">achars</a><sup id="cite_ref-shaheda_410-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shaheda-410">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Chutney" title="Chutney">chutneys</a> are also widely used in the cuisine.<sup id="cite_ref-cuisine_409-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cuisine-409">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 13–14">&#58;&#8202;13–14&#8202;</span></sup>
</p><p>Fish is the main source of protein, owing to the country's <a href="/wiki/River" title="River">riverine</a> geography, and it is often enjoyed with its <a href="/wiki/Roe" title="Roe">roe</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Hilsa" class="mw-redirect" title="Hilsa">hilsa</a> is the national fish and immensely popular, a famous dish is <a href="/wiki/Shorshe_ilish" title="Shorshe ilish">shorshe ilish</a>. <a href="/wiki/Rohu" title="Rohu">Rohu</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pangasius_pangasius" title="Pangasius pangasius">pangas</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Tilapia" title="Tilapia">tilapia</a> are also highly consumed.<sup id="cite_ref-412" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-412">&#91;412&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Lobster" title="Lobster">Lobsters</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shrimp" title="Shrimp">shrimps</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dried_fish" title="Dried fish">dried fish</a> (<i>shutki</i>) are also widely consumed, with the <a href="/wiki/Chingri_malai_curry" title="Chingri malai curry">chingri malai curry</a> being a famous shrimp dish.<sup id="cite_ref-cuisine_409-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cuisine-409">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 8">&#58;&#8202;8&#8202;</span></sup> In Chittagong, famous dishes include <a href="/wiki/Kala_bhuna" title="Kala bhuna">kala bhuna</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mezban" title="Mezban">mezban</a>; the latter being a traditionally popular feast, featuring the serving of <i>mezbani gosht</i>, a hot and spicy beef curry.<sup id="cite_ref-cuisine_409-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cuisine-409">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup><sup class="reference nowrap"><span title="Page / location: 10">&#58;&#8202;10&#8202;</span></sup><sup id="cite_ref-shaheda_410-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shaheda-410">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-guardiancuisine_413-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardiancuisine-413">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup> In Sylhet, the <i><a href="/wiki/Shatkora" class="mw-redirect" title="Shatkora">shatkora</a></i> lemons are used to marinate dishes, a notable one is <a href="/wiki/Beef_Hatkhora" title="Beef Hatkhora">beef hatkora</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-guardiancuisine_413-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardiancuisine-413">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup> Among the tribal communities in the <a href="/wiki/Chittagong_Hill_Tracts" title="Chittagong Hill Tracts">Chittagong Hill Tracts</a>, cooking with <a href="/wiki/Bamboo_shoot" title="Bamboo shoot">bamboo shoots</a> is popular.<sup id="cite_ref-414" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-414">&#91;414&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Khulna_Division" title="Khulna Division">Khulna</a> is renowned for using <i>chui jhal</i> (<a href="/wiki/Piper_chaba" title="Piper chaba">piper chaba</a>) in its meat-based dishes.<sup id="cite_ref-guardiancuisine_413-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardiancuisine-413">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-shaheda_410-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shaheda-410">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh has a vast spread of desserts, including distinctive <a href="/wiki/Sweets" class="mw-redirect" title="Sweets">sweets</a> such as the <i><a href="/wiki/Rasgulla" title="Rasgulla">rôshogolla</a></i>,  <i><a href="/wiki/Ras_malai" title="Ras malai">roshmalai</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Chomchom" title="Chomchom">chomchom</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Sandesh_(confectionery)" title="Sandesh (confectionery)">sondesh</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Mishti_doi" title="Mishti doi">mishti doi</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Gulab_jamun" title="Gulab jamun">kalojaam</a></i>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Jalebi" title="Jalebi">jilapi</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-415" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-415">&#91;415&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Pitha" title="Pitha">Pithas</a> are traditional boiled desserts made with rice or fruits.<sup id="cite_ref-416" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-416">&#91;416&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Halwa" class="mw-redirect" title="Halwa">Halwa</a> is served during religious festivities.<sup id="cite_ref-417" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-417">&#91;417&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Roti" title="Roti">Ruti</a>, <a href="/wiki/Naan" title="Naan">naan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Paratha" title="Paratha">paratha</a>, <a href="/wiki/Luchi" title="Luchi">luchi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Bakarkhani" title="Bakarkhani">bakarkhani</a> are the main local breads.<sup id="cite_ref-418" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-418">&#91;418&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-shaheda_410-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shaheda-410">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup> Hot <a href="/wiki/Milk_tea" title="Milk tea">milk tea</a> is the most commonly consumed beverage in the country, being the centre of <a href="/wiki/Adda_(South_Asian)" title="Adda (South Asian)">addas</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-419" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-419">&#91;419&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Borhani" title="Borhani">Borhani</a> is a popular traditionally consumed beverage.<sup id="cite_ref-420" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-420">&#91;420&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Kebab" title="Kebab">Kebabs</a> are widely popular, particularly <a href="/wiki/Seekh_kebab" title="Seekh kebab">seekh kebab</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chapli_kebab" title="Chapli kebab">chapli kebab</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shami_kebab" title="Shami kebab">shami kebab</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chicken_tikka" title="Chicken tikka">chicken tikka</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shashlik" title="Shashlik">shashlik</a>, along with various types of <i>chaaps</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-shaheda_410-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shaheda-410">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup> Popular street foods include <a href="/wiki/Chotpoti" title="Chotpoti">chotpoti</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jhal_muri" class="mw-redirect" title="Jhal muri">jhal muri</a> and <a href="/wiki/Panipuri" title="Panipuri">fuchka</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-421" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-421">&#91;421&#93;</a></sup> The large Bangladeshi diaspora dominate the South Asian restaurant industry in many Western countries, particularly in the United Kingdom.<sup id="cite_ref-guardiancuisine_413-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardiancuisine-413">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Festivals">Festivals</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Public_holidays_in_Bangladesh" title="Public holidays in Bangladesh">Public holidays in Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_festivals_in_Bangladesh" title="List of festivals in Bangladesh">List of festivals in Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:302px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Nouka_Baich_(Boat_Race)_(9903944955).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Nouka_Baich_%28Boat_Race%29_%289903944955%29.jpg/300px-Nouka_Baich_%28Boat_Race%29_%289903944955%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="199" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Nouka_Baich_%28Boat_Race%29_%289903944955%29.jpg/450px-Nouka_Baich_%28Boat_Race%29_%289903944955%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Nouka_Baich_%28Boat_Race%29_%289903944955%29.jpg/600px-Nouka_Baich_%28Boat_Race%29_%289903944955%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3008" data-file-height="2000" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Nouka_Baich_(Boat_Race)_(9903944955).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>A <a href="/wiki/Nouka_Baich" title="Nouka Baich">Nouka Baich</a> boat race</div></div></div>
<p><i><a href="/wiki/Pahela_Baishakh" class="mw-redirect" title="Pahela Baishakh">Pahela Baishakh</a></i>, the Bengali new year, is the major festival of <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Bengal" title="Culture of Bengal">Bengali culture</a> and sees widespread festivities. Of the major holidays celebrated in Bangladesh, only Pahela Baishakh comes without any pre-existing expectations (specific religious identity, culture of gift-giving, etc.) and has become an occasion for celebrating the simpler, rural roots of the Bengal. Other cultural festivals include <a href="/wiki/Nabanna" title="Nabanna">Nabonno</a> and Poush Parbon, Bengali harvest festivals.
</p><p>The Muslim festivals of Eid al-Fitr, <a href="/wiki/Eid_al-Adha" title="Eid al-Adha">Eid al-Adha</a>, <a href="/wiki/Milad_un_Nabi" class="mw-redirect" title="Milad un Nabi">Milad un Nabi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Muharram" title="Muharram">Muharram</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chand_Raat" class="mw-redirect" title="Chand Raat">Chand Raat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Barat_Night" class="mw-redirect" title="Barat Night">Shab-e-Barat</a>; the Hindu festivals of <a href="/wiki/Durga_Puja" title="Durga Puja">Durga Puja</a>, <a href="/wiki/Janmashtami" class="mw-redirect" title="Janmashtami">Janmashtami</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rath_Yatra" class="mw-redirect" title="Rath Yatra">Rath Yatra</a>; the Buddhist festival of <a href="/wiki/Vesak" title="Vesak">Buddha Purnima</a>, which marks the birth of <a href="/wiki/Gautama_Buddha" class="mw-redirect" title="Gautama Buddha">Gautama Buddha</a>, and the Christian festival of Christmas are <a href="/wiki/Public_holidays_in_Bangladesh" title="Public holidays in Bangladesh">national holidays</a> in Bangladesh and see the most widespread celebrations in the country. The two Eids are celebrated with a long streak of public holidays and give the city-dwellers opportunity to celebrate the festivals with their families outside the city.
</p><p>Alongside are national days like the remembrance of 21 February 1952 <a href="/wiki/Language_Movement_Day" title="Language Movement Day">Language Movement Day</a> (declared as <a href="/wiki/International_Mother_Language_Day" title="International Mother Language Day">International Mother Language Day</a> by <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> in 1999),<sup id="cite_ref-UNESCO_422-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UNESCO-422">&#91;422&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Independence_Day_(Bangladesh)" title="Independence Day (Bangladesh)">Independence Day</a> and <a href="/wiki/Victory_day_of_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Victory day of Bangladesh">Victory Day</a>. On Language Movement Day, people congregate at the <a href="/wiki/Shaheed_Minar,_Dhaka" title="Shaheed Minar, Dhaka">Shaheed Minar</a> in Dhaka to remember the national heroes of the Bengali Language Movement. Similar gatherings are observed at the <a href="/wiki/National_Martyrs%27_Memorial" title="National Martyrs&#39; Memorial">National Martyrs' Memorial</a> on Independence Day and Victory Day to remember the national heroes of the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War" title="Bangladesh Liberation War">Bangladesh Liberation War</a>. These occasions are celebrated with public ceremonies, parades, rallies by citizens, political speeches, fairs, concerts, and various other public and private events, celebrating the history and traditions of Bangladesh. TV and radio stations broadcast special programmes and patriotic songs. Many schools and colleges organise fairs, festivals, and concerts that draw the participation of citizens from all levels of Bangladeshi society.<sup id="cite_ref-423" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-423">&#91;423&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Sports">Sports</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Sports_in_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Sports in Bangladesh">Sports in Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Mashrafe_2016_(9).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Mashrafe_2016_%289%29.jpg/220px-Mashrafe_2016_%289%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Mashrafe_2016_%289%29.jpg/330px-Mashrafe_2016_%289%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Mashrafe_2016_%289%29.jpg/440px-Mashrafe_2016_%289%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2972" data-file-height="1982" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Mashrafe_2016_(9).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_cricket_team" class="mw-redirect" title="Bangladesh cricket team">Bangladesh cricket team</a></div></div></div>
<p>In rural Bangladesh, several <a href="/wiki/Traditional_games_of_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Traditional games of Bangladesh">traditional indigenous sports</a> such as <a href="/wiki/Kabaddi" title="Kabaddi">Kabaddi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Boli_Khela" class="mw-redirect" title="Boli Khela">Boli Khela</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lathi_Khela" class="mw-redirect" title="Lathi Khela">Lathi Khela</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nouka_Baich" title="Nouka Baich">Nouka Baich</a> remain fairly popular. While <a href="/wiki/Kabaddi" title="Kabaddi">Kabaddi</a> is the national sport,<sup id="cite_ref-424" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-424">&#91;424&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Cricket" title="Cricket">cricket</a> is the most popular sport in the country. The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_national_cricket_team" title="Bangladesh national cricket team">national cricket team</a> participated in their first <a href="/wiki/Cricket_World_Cup" title="Cricket World Cup">Cricket World Cup</a> in 1999 and the following year was granted <a href="/wiki/Test_cricket" title="Test cricket">Test cricket</a> status. Bangladesh reached the quarter-final of the <a href="/wiki/2015_Cricket_World_Cup" title="2015 Cricket World Cup">2015 Cricket World Cup</a>, the semi-final of the <a href="/wiki/2017_ICC_Champions_Trophy" title="2017 ICC Champions Trophy">2017 ICC Champions Trophy</a> and they reached the final of the <a href="/wiki/Asia_Cup" title="Asia Cup">Asia Cup</a> 3 times – in 2012, 2016 and 2018. In February 2020, the Bangladesh youth national cricket team won the men's <a href="/wiki/2020_Under-19_Cricket_World_Cup" title="2020 Under-19 Cricket World Cup">Under-19 Cricket World Cup</a>, held in South Africa. This was Bangladesh's first World Cup victory.<sup id="cite_ref-425" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-425">&#91;425&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-426" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-426">&#91;426&#93;</a></sup> Women's sports saw significant progress in the 2010s decade in Bangladesh. In 2018, the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_women%27s_national_cricket_team" title="Bangladesh women&#39;s national cricket team">Bangladesh women's national cricket team</a> won the <a href="/wiki/2018_Women%27s_Twenty20_Asia_Cup" title="2018 Women&#39;s Twenty20 Asia Cup">2018 Women's Twenty20 Asia Cup</a> defeating <a href="/wiki/India_women%27s_national_cricket_team" title="India women&#39;s national cricket team">India women's national cricket team</a> in the final.<sup id="cite_ref-427" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-427">&#91;427&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Football is a major sport in Bangladesh,<sup id="cite_ref-428" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-428">&#91;428&#93;</a></sup> and is governed by the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Football_Federation" title="Bangladesh Football Federation">Bangladesh Football Federation</a> (BFF). Although football was seen as the most popular sport in the country before the 21st century, success in cricket has overshadowed its past popularity. The first instance of a Bangladesh national football team was the emergence of the <a href="/wiki/Shadhin_Bangla_Football_Team" class="mw-redirect" title="Shadhin Bangla Football Team">Shadhin Bangla Football Team</a> that toured throughout <a href="/wiki/India" title="India">India</a> playing a total of 16 friendly matches to raise international awareness about the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War" title="Bangladesh Liberation War">Bangladesh Liberation War</a>, in 1971.<sup id="cite_ref-429" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-429">&#91;429&#93;</a></sup> After independence, the national team also participated in the <a href="/wiki/AFC_Asian_Cup" title="AFC Asian Cup">AFC Asian Cup</a> (<a href="/wiki/1980_AFC_Asian_Cup" title="1980 AFC Asian Cup">1980</a>), becoming only the second <a href="/wiki/South_Asian" class="mw-redirect" title="South Asian">South Asian</a> team to do so.<sup id="cite_ref-430" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-430">&#91;430&#93;</a></sup> Bangladesh's most notable achievements in football include the <a href="/wiki/2003_South_Asian_Football_Federation_Gold_Cup" title="2003 South Asian Football Federation Gold Cup">2003 SAFF Championship</a> and <a href="/wiki/Football_at_the_1999_South_Asian_Games" title="Football at the 1999 South Asian Games">1999 South Asian Games</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_women%27s_national_football_team" title="Bangladesh women&#39;s national football team">Bangladesh women's national football team</a> has also registered some success at regional level, especially the Under-15 and Under-18 teams.<sup id="cite_ref-431" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-431">&#91;431&#93;</a></sup> In 2022, the women's team created history by winning the <a href="/wiki/2022_SAFF_Women%27s_Championship" title="2022 SAFF Women&#39;s Championship">2022 SAFF Women's Championship</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-432" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-432">&#91;432&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-433" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-433">&#91;433&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh archers Ety Khatun and Roman Sana won several gold medals winning all the 10 <a href="/wiki/Archery" title="Archery">archery</a> events (both individual, and team events) in the <a href="/wiki/2019_South_Asian_Games" title="2019 South Asian Games">2019 South Asian Games</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-434" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-434">&#91;434&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/National_Sports_Council" title="National Sports Council">National Sports Council</a> regulates 42 sporting federations.<sup id="cite_ref-435" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-435">&#91;435&#93;</a></sup> Athletics, swimming, archery, boxing, volleyball, weight-lifting and wrestling and different forms of martial arts remain popular. <a href="/wiki/Chess" title="Chess">Chess</a> is very popular in Bangladesh. Bangladesh has five grandmasters in chess. Among them, <a href="/wiki/Niaz_Murshed" title="Niaz Murshed">Niaz Murshed</a> was the first grandmaster in South Asia.<sup id="cite_ref-436" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-436">&#91;436&#93;</a></sup> In 2010, mountain climber <a href="/wiki/Musa_Ibrahim" title="Musa Ibrahim">Musa Ibrahim</a> became the first Bangladeshi climber to conquer <a href="/wiki/Mount_Everest" title="Mount Everest">Mount Everest</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-dailystardetail_437-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dailystardetail-437">&#91;437&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Wasfia_Nazreen" title="Wasfia Nazreen">Wasfia Nazreen</a> is the first Bangladeshi climber to climb the <a href="/wiki/Seven_Summits" title="Seven Summits">Seven Summits</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-438" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-438">&#91;438&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Bangladesh hosts a number of international tournaments. <a href="/wiki/Bangabandhu_Cup" title="Bangabandhu Cup">Bangabandhu Cup</a> is an international football tournament hosted in the country. Bangladesh hosted the South Asian Games several times. In 2011, Bangladesh co-hosted the <a href="/wiki/ICC_Cricket_World_Cup_2011" class="mw-redirect" title="ICC Cricket World Cup 2011">ICC Cricket World Cup 2011</a> with India and Sri Lanka. Bangladesh solely hosted the <a href="/wiki/2014_ICC_World_Twenty20" title="2014 ICC World Twenty20">2014 ICC World Twenty20</a> championship. Bangladesh hosted the <a href="/wiki/Asia_Cup" title="Asia Cup">Asia Cup</a> Cricket Tournament in 2000, 2012, 2014 and 2016.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Media_and_cinema">Media and cinema</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Media_of_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Media of Bangladesh">Media of Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Bangladesh" title="Cinema of Bangladesh">Cinema of Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Anwar_Hossain_in_the_film_%22Nawab_Sirajuddoulah%22_(1967).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Anwar_Hossain_in_the_film_%22Nawab_Sirajuddoulah%22_%281967%29.jpg/220px-Anwar_Hossain_in_the_film_%22Nawab_Sirajuddoulah%22_%281967%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="150" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Anwar_Hossain_in_the_film_%22Nawab_Sirajuddoulah%22_%281967%29.jpg/330px-Anwar_Hossain_in_the_film_%22Nawab_Sirajuddoulah%22_%281967%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Anwar_Hossain_in_the_film_%22Nawab_Sirajuddoulah%22_%281967%29.jpg/440px-Anwar_Hossain_in_the_film_%22Nawab_Sirajuddoulah%22_%281967%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="660" data-file-height="451" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Anwar_Hossain_in_the_film_%22Nawab_Sirajuddoulah%22_(1967).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Anwar_Hossain_(actor)" title="Anwar Hossain (actor)">Anwar Hossain</a> playing <a href="/wiki/Siraj-ud-Daulah" class="mw-redirect" title="Siraj-ud-Daulah">Siraj-ud-Daulah</a>, the last independent <a href="/wiki/Nawab_of_Bengal" class="mw-redirect" title="Nawab of Bengal">Nawab of Bengal</a>, in the 1967 film <i><a href="/wiki/Nawab_Sirajuddaula_(film)" title="Nawab Sirajuddaula (film)">Nawab Sirajuddaulah</a></i></div></div></div>
<p>The Bangladeshi press is diverse, outspoken and privately owned. Over 200 newspapers are published in the country. <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Betar" title="Bangladesh Betar">Bangladesh Betar</a> is the state-run radio service.<sup id="cite_ref-439" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-439">&#91;439&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/British_Broadcasting_Corporation" class="mw-redirect" title="British Broadcasting Corporation">British Broadcasting Corporation</a> operates the popular <a href="/wiki/BBC_Bangla" title="BBC Bangla">BBC Bangla</a> news and current affairs service. Bengali broadcasts from <a href="/wiki/Voice_of_America" title="Voice of America">Voice of America</a> are also very popular. <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Television" title="Bangladesh Television">Bangladesh Television</a> (BTV) is a state-owned television network. More than 20 privately owned television networks, including several <a href="/wiki/News_channel" class="mw-redirect" title="News channel">news channels</a>. <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_the_media" class="mw-redirect" title="Freedom of the media">Freedom of the media</a> remains a major concern due to government attempts at censorship and the harassment of journalists.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Bangladesh" title="Cinema of Bangladesh">cinema of Bangladesh</a> dates back to 1898 when films began screening at the Crown Theatre in Dhaka. The first bioscope on the subcontinent was established in Dhaka that year. The <a href="/wiki/Dhaka_Nawab_Family" class="mw-redirect" title="Dhaka Nawab Family">Dhaka Nawab Family</a> patronised the production of several <a href="/wiki/Silent_film" title="Silent film">silent films</a> in the 1920s and 30s. In 1931, the East Bengal Cinematograph Society released the first full-length feature film in Bangladesh, titled the <i>Last Kiss</i>. The first feature film in East Pakistan, <i><a href="/wiki/Mukh_O_Mukhosh" title="Mukh O Mukhosh">Mukh O Mukhosh</a></i>, was released in 1956. During the 1960s, 25–30 films were produced annually in Dhaka. By the 2000s, Bangladesh produced 80–100 films a year. While the Bangladeshi film industry has achieved limited commercial success, the country has produced notable independent filmmakers. <a href="/wiki/Zahir_Raihan" title="Zahir Raihan">Zahir Raihan</a> was a prominent documentary-maker assassinated in 1971. The late <a href="/wiki/Tareque_Masud" title="Tareque Masud">Tareque Masud</a> is regarded as one of Bangladesh's outstanding directors for his critically acclaimed films on social issues.<sup id="cite_ref-440" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-440">&#91;440&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-441" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-441">&#91;441&#93;</a></sup> Masud was honoured by <a href="/wiki/FIPRESCI" class="mw-redirect" title="FIPRESCI">FIPRESCI</a> at the 2002 <a href="/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival" title="Cannes Film Festival">Cannes Film Festival</a> for his film <i><a href="/wiki/Matir_Moina" title="Matir Moina">The Clay Bird</a></i>. <a href="/wiki/Tanvir_Mokammel" title="Tanvir Mokammel">Tanvir Mokammel</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mostofa_Sarwar_Farooki" title="Mostofa Sarwar Farooki">Mostofa Sarwar Farooki</a>, <a href="/wiki/Humayun_Ahmed" title="Humayun Ahmed">Humayun Ahmed</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alamgir_Kabir_(filmmaker)" class="mw-redirect" title="Alamgir Kabir (filmmaker)">Alamgir Kabir</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Chashi_Nazrul_Islam" title="Chashi Nazrul Islam">Chashi Nazrul Islam</a> are some of the prominent directors of Bangladeshi cinema. Bangladesh has a very active film society culture. It started in 1963 in Dhaka. Now around 40 Film Societies are active all over Bangladesh. <a href="/wiki/Federation_of_Film_Societies_of_Bangladesh" title="Federation of Film Societies of Bangladesh">Federation of Film Societies of Bangladesh</a> is the parent organisation of the film society movement of Bangladesh. Active film societies include the Rainbow Film Society, <a href="/wiki/Children%27s_Film_Society" class="mw-redirect" title="Children&#39;s Film Society">Children's Film Society</a>, <a href="/wiki/Moviyana_Film_Society" title="Moviyana Film Society">Moviyana Film Society</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dhaka_University_Film_Society" title="Dhaka University Film Society">Dhaka University Film Society</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Museums_and_libraries">Museums and libraries</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Museums_in_Bangladesh" class="mw-redirect" title="Museums in Bangladesh">Museums in Bangladesh</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_libraries_in_Bangladesh" title="List of libraries in Bangladesh">List of libraries in Bangladesh</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Varendra_Research_Museum_10.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Varendra_Research_Museum_10.jpg/220px-Varendra_Research_Museum_10.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="124" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Varendra_Research_Museum_10.jpg/330px-Varendra_Research_Museum_10.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Varendra_Research_Museum_10.jpg/440px-Varendra_Research_Museum_10.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4208" data-file-height="2368" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Varendra_Research_Museum_10.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Varendra_Research_Museum" title="Varendra Research Museum">Varendra Research Museum</a> in <a href="/wiki/Rajshahi" title="Rajshahi">Rajshahi</a> is the oldest surviving museum in Bangladesh</div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Varendra_Research_Museum" title="Varendra Research Museum">Varendra Research Museum</a> is the oldest museum in Bangladesh. It houses important collections from both the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods, including the sculptures of the Pala-Sena School of Art and the Indus Valley civilisation, and Sanskrit, Arabic, and Persian manuscripts and inscriptions. The Ahsan Manzil, the former residence of the Nawab of Dhaka, is a national museum housing collections from the British Raj. It was the site of the founding conference of the All India Muslim League and hosted many British Viceroys in Dhaka.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Tajhat_Palace" title="Tajhat Palace">Tajhat Palace</a> Museum preserves artefacts of the rich cultural heritage of North Bengal, including Hindu-Buddhist sculptures and Islamic manuscripts. The <a href="/wiki/Mymensingh_Museum" title="Mymensingh Museum">Mymensingh Museum</a> houses the personal antique collections of Bengali aristocrats in central Bengal. The <a href="/wiki/Ethnological_Museum_of_Chittagong" class="mw-redirect" title="Ethnological Museum of Chittagong">Ethnological Museum of Chittagong</a> showcases the lifestyle of various tribes in Bangladesh. The <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_National_Museum" title="Bangladesh National Museum">Bangladesh National Museum</a> is located in <a href="/wiki/Ramna" class="mw-redirect" title="Ramna">Ramna</a>, Dhaka and has a rich collection of antiquities. The <a href="/wiki/Liberation_War_Museum" title="Liberation War Museum">Liberation War Museum</a> documents the Bangladeshi struggle for independence and the 1971 genocide.
</p><p>In ancient times, manuscripts were written on palm leaves, tree barks, parchment vellum and terracotta plates and preserved at monasteries known as <i><a href="/wiki/Vihara" class="mw-redirect" title="Vihara">viharas</a></i>. The Hussain Shahi dynasty established royal libraries during the Bengal Sultanate. Libraries were established in each district of Bengal by the zamindar gentry during the Bengal Renaissance in the 19th century. The trend of establishing libraries continued until the beginning of World War II. In 1854, four major public libraries were opened, including the Bogra Woodburn Library, the Rangpur Public Library, the Jessore Institute Public Library and the Barisal Public Library.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Northbrook_Hall" title="Northbrook Hall">Northbrook Hall Public Library</a> was established in Dhaka in 1882 in honour of <a href="/wiki/Lord_Northbrook" class="mw-redirect" title="Lord Northbrook">Lord Northbrook</a>, the Governor-General. Other libraries established in the British period included the Victoria Public Library, Natore (1901), the Sirajganj Public Library (1882), the <a href="/wiki/Rajshahi_Public_Library" title="Rajshahi Public Library">Rajshahi Public Library</a> (1884), the Comilla Birchandra Library (1885), the Shah Makhdum Institute Public Library, Rajshahi (1891), the Noakhali Town Hall Public Library (1896), the Prize Memorial Library, Sylhet (1897), the Chittagong Municipality Public Library (1904) and the Varendra Research Library (1910). The Great Bengal Library Association was formed in 1925.<sup id="cite_ref-442" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-442">&#91;442&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Central_Public_Library_(Dhaka)" class="mw-redirect" title="Central Public Library (Dhaka)">Central Public Library of Dhaka</a> was established in 1959. The <a href="/wiki/National_Library_of_Bangladesh" title="National Library of Bangladesh">National Library of Bangladesh</a> was established in 1972. The <a href="/wiki/Bishwo_Shahitto_Kendro" title="Bishwo Shahitto Kendro">World Literature Centre</a>, founded by <a href="/wiki/Ramon_Magsaysay_Award" title="Ramon Magsaysay Award">Ramon Magsaysay Award</a> winner <a href="/wiki/Abdullah_Abu_Sayeed" title="Abdullah Abu Sayeed">Abdullah Abu Sayeed</a>, is noted for operating numerous <a href="/wiki/Mobile_library" class="mw-redirect" title="Mobile library">mobile libraries</a> across Bangladesh and was awarded the UNESCO Jon, Amos Comenius Medal.
</p>
